title.rendered: Download the Official MacBook Neo Wallpapers in 4K

content.rendered:
Apple recently introduced the MacBook Neo, a new budget-friendly MacBook offering the same premium macOS experience. As per tradition, it comes with a fresh set of colorful default wallpapers. If you love Apple’s minimalist design language, you can now download the official MacBook Neo wallpapers in 4K resolution and use them on any device.

In this article, you’ll find details about the wallpapers, including their resolution, available colors, and instructions on how to download them in full quality.

Table of Contents
  • MacBook Neo Wallpapers: Overview
  • Download the Official MacBook Neo Wallpapers
  • Why MacBook Neo Wallpapers Look So Good
    • Final Thoughts

MacBook Neo Wallpapers: Overview

The MacBook Neo ships with four new stock wallpapers designed to match the device’s aluminum finish options: Blush, Indigo, Silver, and Citrus. According to Apple, Neo stands for “something that felt fun and friendly, and fresh.” And indeed, the wallpapers look playful, energetic, yet premium.

They feature a modern, geometric design composed of subtle, translucent vertical shapes and spheres that create depth and complement Apple’s minimalist aesthetic. If you look closely, you will notice that the shapes spell “MAC.”

Apple created these wallpapers at 6016 x 6016 pixels (5K resolution), ensuring crisp visuals even on large displays.

Download the Official MacBook Neo Wallpapers

The new set of MacBook Neo wallpapers is available to all Macs with the fourth beta of macOS Tahoe 26.4. However, if you haven’t updated yet, here are the wallpapers in the highest resolutions. Simply, scroll down and hit the Download button to save them to your device.

Download: Indigo | Silver | Blush | Citrus

Why MacBook Neo Wallpapers Look So Good

Apple carefully designs its wallpapers to enhance the visual experience of its devices. The MacBook Neo wallpapers use:

  • Layered geometric shapes
  • Color-matched gradients
  • Subtle lighting and transparency effects

These design elements complement macOS Tahoe’s Liquid Glass aesthetics and help icons remain clear while making the desktop visually appealing.

The MacBook Neo offers powerful performance in a sleek and portable design. Pairing it with the right accessories can improve productivity, connectivity, and protection.

Final Thoughts

The MacBook Neo wallpapers are a great addition to Apple’s stock wallpaper collection. With bright color options like Blush, Indigo, Silver, and vibrant Citrus, these backgrounds can give your desktop a modern and premium feel.

Due to their Retina quality, they will look great on everything from laptops to large 4K and 5K monitors. If you like Apple’s clean and colorful style, these wallpapers are definitely worth downloading.

  • MacBook Neo: The Best Reasons to Buy and the Biggest Reasons to Skip
  • Best MacBook Neo Sleeves

mainEntity.name: Can all Apple Watches use Precision Finding for AirTags?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Only Apple Watch Series 9 and later, and Apple Watch Ultra 2 and later models running iOS 26.2.1, can use Precision Finding. Older models may still show the AirTag’s location in the Maps in Find Items app, but won’t provide directional guidance.

mainEntity.name: Do you need an iPhone nearby?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Your Apple Watch must remain paired with an iPhone that is connected to the same Apple ID. The iPhone helps manage the connection to the Find My network.

mainEntity.name: How accurate is Precision Finding on Apple Watch?

acceptedAnswer.text: Precision Finding is extremely accurate when you are close to the AirTag. It can guide you within a few feet of the item using directional arrows, distance tracking, and haptic feedback.

title.rendered: How to Make Your Old iPhone Feel Faster Without Buying a New One

content.rendered:
If your iPhone feels slower than it used to, but you are not ready to spend money on a new one, you are not alone. Many people hold on to their devices for years, and with the right adjustments, an older iPhone can still run smoothly. It will not magically turn into the latest model, but it can absolutely feel faster, cleaner, and more responsive.

Before we begin, it is important to stay realistic. Software tweaks help, but they cannot overcome hardware limits. Older processors, smaller RAM, and aging batteries all play a role. Still, most slowdowns come from clutter, background activity, and poor optimization, and those can be fixed.

Table of Contents
  • 1. Update Your iPhone’s Software
  • 2. Free Up Storage Space
  • 3. Disable Background App Refresh
  • 4. Reduce Motion and Transparency
  • 5. Optimize Location Services
  • 6. Restart Your iPhone Weekly
  • 7. Limit Widgets and Home Screen Pages
  • 8. Check Battery Health
  • 9. Consider a Factory Reset
  • Performance Is Mostly About Optimization
  • Final Thoughts

1. Update Your iPhone’s Software

Software updates are not just about new features. Apple often improves memory management, fixes bugs, and patches performance issues in each iOS release.

  1. Open Settings.
  2. Tap General.
  3. Tap Software Update.
  4. If an update is available, tap Update Now (plug in your iPhone if the battery is low).
  5. Follow the on-screen prompts and let your iPhone restart.

However, do not update blindly. Some very old models struggle with feature-heavy releases. Before installing, check user feedback for your specific iPhone model on forums or Reddit. If users report lag, it may be wise to wait.

2. Free Up Storage Space

Storage plays a huge role in performance. When your iPhone is nearly full, it struggles to manage temporary files and background tasks. Try to keep at least 10 to 20 percent of storage free.

  1. Open Settings.
  2. Tap General.
  3. Tap iPhone Storage.
  4. Review what is taking up space and follow any recommendations shown at the top.

Photos and videos are usually the biggest problem. You can delete them manually, enable Optimize iPhone Storage in iCloud settings, or use a cleaning app to sort large files faster.

Many cleaning apps today use AI to detect similar images, screenshots, duplicate photos, and large videos. This makes cleanup much easier than scrolling through thousands of pictures manually. Always check the app’s privacy policy to ensure processing happens locally on your device.

After cleaning media, review apps. Delete unused ones or use the Offload App option to remove the app but keep its data.

3. Disable Background App Refresh

Background App Refresh allows apps to update content even when you are not using them. This consumes RAM, CPU power, and battery.

  1. Open Settings.
  2. Tap General.
  3. Tap Background App Refresh.
  4. Choose Off to disable it completely, or leave it on and toggle it off for non-essential apps.

Keep it enabled only for apps that truly need constant updates, like messaging or email.

4. Reduce Motion and Transparency

Animations and visual effects look beautiful, but use system resources.

  1. Open Settings.
  2. Tap Accessibility.
  3. Tap Motion.
  4. Turn on Reduce Motion.
  5. Go back, tap Display & Text Size.
  6. Turn on Reduce Transparency.

These changes reduce GPU workload and can make older iPhones feel noticeably snappier.

5. Optimize Location Services

Location tracking runs quietly in the background and drains resources.

  1. Open Settings.
  2. Tap Privacy & Security.
  3. Tap Location Services.
  4. For most apps, switch access to While Using the App or Never.
  5. Scroll down and tap System Services.
  6. Turn off non-essential items like location-based ads and suggestions.

If an app stops working as expected, you can always return here and adjust its permissions.

Less background tracking equals better performance and battery life.

6. Restart Your iPhone Weekly

Restarting clears temporary files and refreshes memory. It is simple but surprisingly effective.

  1. Press and hold the Side button and either Volume button until the power slider appears. (On iPhones with a Home button, press and hold the Power button.)
  2. Drag the slider to power off.
  3. Wait 10–15 seconds.
  4. Press and hold the Side/Power button again until the Apple logo appears.

Doing this once a week helps prevent memory buildup from apps that do not close properly.

7. Limit Widgets and Home Screen Pages

Widgets constantly refresh data. Too many can slow down older devices.

  1. Press and hold an empty area on your Home Screen until icons start to jiggle.
  2. Tap the minus (–) on widgets you do not need, or drag them off the Home Screen.
  3. Drag apps into folders to reduce the number of pages.
  4. Tap Done to save.

A simpler layout reduces background workload and improves responsiveness.

8. Check Battery Health

A worn battery can cause performance throttling. iOS reduces processor speed to prevent unexpected shutdowns.

  1. Open Settings.
  2. Tap Battery.
  3. Tap Battery Health.
  4. Check Maximum Capacity.
  5. Go back and tap Charging.
  6. Turn on Optimized Battery Charging to slow future battery wear.

If the maximum capacity is significantly reduced and performance management is active, a battery replacement can restore full speed. This is often cheaper than buying a new phone and can make a dramatic difference.

9. Consider a Factory Reset

If your phone still feels slow after everything else, a factory reset can remove years of accumulated clutter.

  1. Back up your iPhone with iCloud or a computer first.
  2. Open Settings.
  3. Tap General.
  4. Tap Transfer or Reset iPhone.
  5. Tap Erase All Content and Settings.
  6. Enter your passcode and Apple ID password if prompted.
  7. After the reset, set up as new or restore from your backup.

This will not downgrade iOS, but it removes hidden junk and software conflicts that build up over time.

Performance Is Mostly About Optimization

Most people assume slow phones mean weak hardware. In reality, performance is usually about efficiency. Apps that use too much memory, poor background management, and unnecessary visual effects create slowdowns.

This idea applies beyond smartphones. When companies experience performance bottlenecks in their applications, they often bring in experienced engineers to audit and optimize systems. Many businesses work with nearshore software development teams to modernize platforms and improve efficiency without rebuilding everything from scratch. Others rely on staff augmentation models to temporarily add specialized engineers who fix bottlenecks and improve architecture.

Whether it is an iPhone or a large software platform, speed depends on clean systems, efficient code, and smart resource management.

Final Thoughts

Start simple. Free storage. Disable unnecessary background features. Reduce visual effects. Check battery health.

You do not need to rush into buying a new phone. With a little cleanup and smart adjustments, your old iPhone can feel fast enough to serve you well for another year or two.

Small optimizations add up. And sometimes, that is all your device really needs.

mainEntity.name: Can all Apple Watches use Precision Finding for AirTags?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Only Apple Watch Series 9 and later, and Apple Watch Ultra 2 and later models running iOS 26.2.1, can use Precision Finding. Older models may still show the AirTag’s location in the Maps in Find Items app, but won’t provide directional guidance.

mainEntity.name: Do you need an iPhone nearby?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Your Apple Watch must remain paired with an iPhone that is connected to the same Apple ID. The iPhone helps manage the connection to the Find My network.

mainEntity.name: How accurate is Precision Finding on Apple Watch?

acceptedAnswer.text: Precision Finding is extremely accurate when you are close to the AirTag. It can guide you within a few feet of the item using directional arrows, distance tracking, and haptic feedback.

title.rendered: All Roblox Game Codes: Master List

content.rendered:
Keeping track of Roblox game codes is harder than it sounds.

New experiences launch constantly. Existing games push updates, add new characters, release events, and rebalance mechanics. And almost every meaningful update comes with something players care about, redeemable in-game codes. These codes can unlock spins, rerolls, currency, stat resets, boosts, cosmetics, or limited-time rewards. Some stay active for weeks. Others disappear quietly within days.

If you play multiple Roblox experiences, checking each game individually wastes time. That is why this page exists.

This article is a centralized index of every individual Roblox game code guide we currently cover. If a game is listed below, we actively track its in-game codes, update them when new ones drop, and remove them once they expire.

Complete List of Roblox Game Code Guides

Below is the full list of the Roblox game code pages we cover:

  • All Star Tower Defense X Codes
  • Anime Ascendants Codes

V

W

0 – 9

  • 99 Nights in the Forest Codes

How Game Codes Typically Work

Most Roblox games include a built-in redemption system inside the experience. You will usually find a “Codes” button, a gift icon, or a social media icon on the main interface. Enter the code exactly as shown and press redeem. If it is active, rewards apply instantly. If it says expired or invalid, the developer has disabled it.

Developers release codes for several common reasons:

  • Major content updates
  • Milestone celebrations (likes, visits, followers)
  • Balance changes or reworks
  • Seasonal or limited-time events
  • Compensation after bugs or server issues

Because these codes are tied to update cycles, they can expire without warning.

Why This Master List Matters

Roblox is not a single evolving game. It is thousands of independent ecosystems running simultaneously. Each one has its own progression system and reward structure. If you are not redeeming codes, you are progressing slower than necessary.

This master list serves as your central hub. If the game you play appears above, you can access its dedicated code guide and claim rewards before they disappear.

mainEntity.name: Can all Apple Watches use Precision Finding for AirTags?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Only Apple Watch Series 9 and later, and Apple Watch Ultra 2 and later models running iOS 26.2.1, can use Precision Finding. Older models may still show the AirTag’s location in the Maps in Find Items app, but won’t provide directional guidance.

mainEntity.name: Do you need an iPhone nearby?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Your Apple Watch must remain paired with an iPhone that is connected to the same Apple ID. The iPhone helps manage the connection to the Find My network.

mainEntity.name: How accurate is Precision Finding on Apple Watch?

acceptedAnswer.text: Precision Finding is extremely accurate when you are close to the AirTag. It can guide you within a few feet of the item using directional arrows, distance tracking, and haptic feedback.

title.rendered: Buy iPhone 17e Now or Wait for iPhone 18? Here’s What You Should Do

content.rendered:
Apple recently released its new affordable iPhone, the iPhone 17e, bringing the iPhone 17 series to a more accessible price point. If you are planning to upgrade your iPhone this year, the iPhone 17e may already be on your radar. However, the timing of its release also raises an important question: Apple’s next flagship lineup, the iPhone 18 series, is expected to arrive later this year.

Because of this, many buyers find themselves wondering, “Should I buy the iPhone 17e now or wait for the iPhone 18?”

To help you decide, we break down what the iPhone 17e offers, what the iPhone 18 could bring, and which option makes more sense for you.

Table of Contents
  • What the iPhone 17e Offers Right Now
    • iPhone 17e Specifications at a Glance
  • What We Expect From the iPhone 18
  • When Buying the iPhone 17e Right Now Makes the Most Sense
  • When It’s Better to Wait for the iPhone 18
  • Should You Buy the iPhone 17e or Wait for the iPhone 18? (Quick Decision Guide)
  • Summing Up

What the iPhone 17e Offers Right Now

Aside from the secondary rear camera and Dynamic Island, the iPhone 17e delivers most modern iPhone features at a more accessible price point. It also retains a compact, lightweight design that many users still prefer over larger smartphones.

Building on the iPhone 16e‘s success, the iPhone 17e offers the solid performance of the A19 chip, an upgraded 48 MP main camera, and long-term software support, making it a strong option for users upgrading from older iPhones.

The phone also offers improved battery life compared to its predecessor, along with MagSafe support for wireless accessories and charging.

iPhone 17e Specifications at a Glance

  • Display: 6.1-inch Super Retina XDR OLED display
  • Chip: A19 chip with improved performance and efficiency
  • Camera: 48 MP main camera with advanced computational photography
  • Front Camera: 12 MP TrueDepth camera
  • Storage: Starts at 128 GB
  • Connectivity: 5G support and Wi-Fi 6E
  • Charging: MagSafe and wireless charging support
  • Software: Ships with the latest version of iOS 26 with long-term update support
  • Design: Compact and lightweight aluminum design
  • Security: Face ID authentication

What We Expect From the iPhone 18

Apple is expected to introduce the iPhone 18 lineup around its usual fall launch window. However, recent rumors suggest the company may split the release schedule this time. According to these reports, the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max could launch later this year, while the standard iPhone 18 might arrive a few months later in spring 2027.

While nothing is officially confirmed yet, the next-generation iPhones are expected to bring improvements across several areas.

Possible upgrades could include:

  • A newer A-series chip with better efficiency and AI capabilities
  • Camera improvements and computational photography upgrades
  • Display enhancements such as improved brightness or refresh technology
  • A smaller Dynamic Island
  • Longer battery life due to a more efficient processor
  • Additional Apple Intelligence features

However, most upgrades will likely appear first in the Pro models, with the standard models receiving more modest improvements.

When Buying the iPhone 17e Right Now Makes the Most Sense

With the standard iPhone 18 now rumored to arrive in spring 2027, buying the iPhone 17e can be the right choice in several situations.

1. Your Current iPhone Is Very Old

If you are using an iPhone that is four or five years old, the performance difference alone will make the upgrade worthwhile. Waiting several more months may not be practical.

2. You Want the Best Value Right Now

The “e” models are usually priced lower than Apple’s flagship devices. If you want a modern iPhone without paying a premium price and are okay with the notch display, the iPhone 17e offers strong value.

3. You Prefer a Compact iPhone

The iPhone 17e retains a compact, lightweight design that many users still appreciate. If you prefer a phone that is easier to hold and use with one hand compared to larger Pro models, the iPhone 17e can be a comfortable and practical choice.

4. You Need a Phone Immediately

If your current device has battery issues, storage limitations, or performance problems, buying the iPhone 17e now solves the problem instantly at a relatively lower cost.

When It’s Better to Wait for the iPhone 18

Although rumors suggest the iPhone 18 is still some time away, there is no guarantee the timeline will remain unchanged. Even if the schedule shifts, waiting for the next generation may still make sense for some buyers.

1. You Already Have a Recent iPhone

If you are currently using an iPhone 15 or iPhone 16, upgrading to the iPhone 17e may feel like a downgrade rather than an upgrade. Waiting for the iPhone 18 could provide more noticeable improvements.

2. You Want the Latest Technology

Apple typically introduces its biggest upgrades in the newest flagship models. If you want the newest processor, camera improvements, and future-focused features, waiting can be worthwhile.

3. You Want Prices to Drop

When Apple launches a new iPhone generation, older models usually become cheaper. Waiting could allow you to buy the iPhone 17 Pro models at a lower price.

Should You Buy the iPhone 17e or Wait for the iPhone 18? (Quick Decision Guide)

Here’s a quick way to decide which option makes more sense for you.

Summing Up

The iPhone 17e is a solid choice if you currently own an older iPhone model, such as the iPhone 11 or iPhone 12, and want a modern iPhone without paying flagship prices. It offers strong performance, a capable camera, and long software support.

However, if your current iPhone still works well and you prefer owning the newest generation, waiting for the iPhone 18 may make more sense.

In the end, the best choice depends on how urgently you need an upgrade and how important the latest features are to you.

Would you buy the iPhone 17e now or wait for the iPhone 18? Share your thoughts in the comments.

excerpt.rendered: Thinking about upgrading your iPhone? The iPhone 17e offers strong performance and great value today, but the upcoming iPhone 18 could bring newer features. Here’s how to decide which one is right for you.

mainEntity.name: Can all Apple Watches use Precision Finding for AirTags?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Only Apple Watch Series 9 and later, and Apple Watch Ultra 2 and later models running iOS 26.2.1, can use Precision Finding. Older models may still show the AirTag’s location in the Maps in Find Items app, but won’t provide directional guidance.

mainEntity.name: Do you need an iPhone nearby?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Your Apple Watch must remain paired with an iPhone that is connected to the same Apple ID. The iPhone helps manage the connection to the Find My network.

mainEntity.name: How accurate is Precision Finding on Apple Watch?

acceptedAnswer.text: Precision Finding is extremely accurate when you are close to the AirTag. It can guide you within a few feet of the item using directional arrows, distance tracking, and haptic feedback.

title.rendered: iMessage vs SMS: Key Differences You Need to Know

content.rendered:
Apple has recently started supporting RCS messaging on iPhone, but the feature is currently limited to devices running iOS 18 and depends on carrier support. Because of this, most iPhone users still rely primarily on iMessage or SMS for their everyday conversations.

If you are a new iPhone user, you may have noticed that some chats in the Messages app appear in blue bubbles, while others appear in green. This often leads to confusion about why your iPhone sends messages in different formats. In simple terms, the bubble color shows which messaging service your iPhone is using.

Keep reading to learn everything you need to know about iMessage vs SMS on iPhone.

Table of Contents
  • What is iMessage?
  • What is SMS?
  • iMessage vs SMS: Key Differences
  • How iPhone Decides Between iMessage and SMS
  • Why Messages Appear in Blue and Green Bubbles?
  • iMessage vs SMS Explained…

What is iMessage?

iMessage is Apple’s proprietary messaging technology designed for communication between Apple devices such as iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Apple Watch.

Unlike traditional SMS, iMessage uses internet connectivity (Wi-Fi or cellular data) to send and receive messages via Apple’s servers. Additionally, Messages sent through iMessage appear in blue chat bubbles in the Messages app, making it easier to differentiate between iMessage, SMS, and RCS messages.

It offers several advanced messaging features, including but not limited to:

  • End-to-end encryption
  • High-resolution photo and video sharing
  • Typing indicators
  • Read receipts
  • Message reactions and effects
  • Stickers and iMessage apps
  • Seamless syncing across Apple devices

What is SMS?

SMS (Short Message Service) is a traditional text messaging standard used by cellular networks worldwide. Unlike iMessage, SMS does not require an internet connection and is sent through your mobile carrier’s cellular network.

On iPhone, SMS messages appear in green bubbles in the Messages app because they are sent through the carrier’s messaging network rather than Apple’s iMessage service.

Key features:

  • Works between any mobile phones, including Android devices
  • Uses the cellular carrier network
  • Requires a mobile signal but not internet
  • Limited to text messages only
  • Media support is limited and usually compressed
  • No read receipts or typing indicators

iMessage vs SMS: Key Differences

Although both services allow you to send messages, the technologies behind them are very different.

How iPhone Decides Between iMessage and SMS

Since the iPhone’s Messages app supports both iMessage and SMS, it automatically checks several factors before deciding which messaging service to use.

1. If the Recipient Uses iMessage

Your iPhone first checks Apple’s servers to see if the recipient’s phone number or email address is registered with iMessage. If it is, the message is sent as an iMessage over Wi-Fi or mobile data. In this case, the message appears in a blue bubble.

2. If the Recipient Does Not Use an Apple Device

If the recipient is using a non-Apple device, such as an Android phone, iMessage cannot be used. Your iPhone automatically sends the message as SMS through your carrier network. These messages appear in green bubbles.

3. If Internet Connectivity Is Unavailable

iMessage requires an internet connection. If your iPhone does not have access& to Wi-Fi or mobile data, it cannot send an iMessage. In this situation, your iPhone sends the message as SMS using your cellular network.

4. When iMessage Fails to Deliver

Sometimes an iMessage may fail due to poor connectivity or server issues. If the Send as SMS option is enabled in your Messages settings, the iPhone can automatically resend the message as SMS.

Why Messages Appear in Blue and Green Bubbles?

Apple’s Messages app uses blue and green bubbles to show which messaging service is used to send and receive them.

Blue bubbles represent iMessage. They indicate that the message is sent via Apple’s iMessage service over an internet connection, such as Wi-Fi or mobile data. This occurs when both you and the recipient are using Apple devices with iMessage enabled.

Green bubbles represent SMS or MMS. They indicate that the message is sent through your cellular carrier’s texting network instead of Apple’s internet-based messaging system. This usually happens when you message someone using a non-Apple device, such as an Android phone, or when iMessage is unavailable.

This visual distinction also signals the features available in a conversation. Blue bubble chats support advanced features like read receipts, typing indicators, and higher-quality media sharing. Green bubble messages are limited to basic text messaging and standard multimedia.

iMessage vs SMS Explained…

Understanding the differences between iMessage and SMS helps you see how your iPhone sends messages and which features are available in each conversation. iMessage uses an internet connection and supports advanced messaging features, while SMS relies on your carrier’s cellular network and supports basic texting. Knowing this makes it easier to understand why your messages behave differently in the Messages app.

Have something to add about iMessage or SMS on iPhone? Share your thoughts in the comments.

Read more:

  • Best iMessage tips and tricks for iPhone users
  • How to change iMessage bubble color on iPhone and iPad

mainEntity.name: Can all Apple Watches use Precision Finding for AirTags?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Only Apple Watch Series 9 and later, and Apple Watch Ultra 2 and later models running iOS 26.2.1, can use Precision Finding. Older models may still show the AirTag’s location in the Maps in Find Items app, but won’t provide directional guidance.

mainEntity.name: Do you need an iPhone nearby?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Your Apple Watch must remain paired with an iPhone that is connected to the same Apple ID. The iPhone helps manage the connection to the Find My network.

mainEntity.name: How accurate is Precision Finding on Apple Watch?

acceptedAnswer.text: Precision Finding is extremely accurate when you are close to the AirTag. It can guide you within a few feet of the item using directional arrows, distance tracking, and haptic feedback.

"Vikhyat has a bachelor’s degree in Electronic and Communication Engineering and over five years of writing experience. His passion for technology and Apple products led him to the tech writing space, where he specializes in writing App features, How-to guides, and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple users. When not typing away on his MacBook Pro, he loves exploring the real world."

 

About Vikhyat Rishi

  • Vikhyat has over five years of experience writing consumer tech content.
  • During his association with Smartprix and Beebom, Vikhyat has tested, tested, and reviewed numerous gadgets, including but not limited to smartphones, TVs, and more.
  • His passion for technology and Apple products led him to iGeeksBlog, where he specializes in writing How-to and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple enthusiasts.

Experience

Vikhyat embarked on his journey in consumer technology writing in 2019, driven by his passion for technology. He has sharpened his skills through associations with Smartprix and Beebom, where he extensively tested and reviewed various gadgets, focusing mainly on smartphones. Currently, Vikhyat specializes in crafting How-to and troubleshooting guides for the Apple ecosystem at iGeeksBlog. When not typing away on his MacBook Air, he loves exploring the real world.

title.rendered: Best iPad to Buy in 2026: Find Your Perfect Match!

content.rendered:
From the budget-friendly iPad (11th gen) to the high-end M5 iPad Pro, Apple offers a wide range of iPad models. So, finding the best iPad to buy can be challenging. In this guide, I’ll explain the key factors to consider when buying an iPad and help you choose the iPad that best meets your requirements and budget. Let’s begin!

Table of Contents
  • Overview of iPad Models in 2026
    • Current iPad Lineup (2026)
    • Upcoming iPad Models (2026):
  • Who Should Buy Which iPad Model?
  • Key Factors to Consider When Choosing an iPad
    • Performance
    • Display
    • iPadOS Support
    • Battery Life
    • Portability and Accessories
    • Apple Intelligence
    • Budget
  • Best iPad for Most People: 2025 iPad (A16)
  • Best iPad for Creators: 2025 iPad Pro M5
  • Best iPad for Professionals: 2026 iPad Air M4
  • Best iPad for Students: 2024 iPad mini
  • When and Where to Buy an iPad in 2026?
  • Pick the Right iPad for You!

Overview of iPad Models in 2026

As of 2026, Apple’s iPad family includes four different lineups: iPad Pro, iPad Air, iPad, and iPad mini. The Pro version offers top-tier performance and advanced features designed for power users and creators. On the other hand, the Air lineup delivers performance in a thin, light design, making it suitable for professionals and businesspeople.

The standard model is best for everyday tasks and suits most people. And finally, the compact iPad mini remains a favorite among users seeking portability without sacrificing functionality.

Current iPad Lineup (2026)

All iPad models are available in two configurations: Wi-Fi and Wi-Fi + Cellular. Here is a quick overview of the iPads available to buy right now:

Upcoming iPad Models (2026):

Who Should Buy Which iPad Model?

  • Best iPad for everyday user: 2025 iPad (A16)
  • Best iPad for creators: 2025 iPad Pro M5
  • Best iPad for professionals: 2026 iPad Air M4
  • Best iPad for students: 2024 iPad mini

Key Factors to Consider When Choosing an iPad

Selecting the right iPad in 2026 depends on your needs, budget, and how you plan to use the device. Apple offers a range of models with different features, so it’s important to evaluate which features matter most to you. Below are the key factors to consider before making your decision.

Performance

The processor determines how smoothly your iPad runs applications, handles multitasking, and maintains overall efficiency. Apple has equipped different iPad models with various chips to suit different needs.

  • A16 Chip (iPad 11th Gen): Ideal for everyday tasks like browsing, social media, streaming, and light productivity work.
  • M4 Chip (iPad Air 8th Gen): A powerful choice for professionals and students who need more speed for multitasking, document editing, and casual creative work.
  • M5 Chip (iPad Pro 8th Gen): The top-tier option for professionals, creators, and power users who require high performance for 3D modeling, video editing, and demanding apps.
  • A17 Pro Chip (iPad mini 7th Gen): Designed for portability without compromising on performance, perfect for reading, note-taking, and on-the-go work.

If you need an iPad for basic tasks, the A16 or A17 Pro chip is more than sufficient. However, if you’re a creator or professional working with heavy apps, an M4 or M5 chip will provide a much smoother experience.

Display

The display size and quality can significantly impact your user experience, whether you’re watching movies, reading, or using the Apple Pencil for creative work. The iPad mini’s compact display is ideal for portability, while the iPad Air’s larger screen is well-suited for creative work and media consumption.

Moreover, the iPad Pro features an Ultra Retina XDR display and ProMotion technology for an immersive experience. For more clarity, you may also opt for the Nano-texture display glass option, which costs a bit more.

iPadOS Support

Software updates are crucial for keeping your device secure and up to date with the latest features. Apple typically provides long-term iPadOS support, ensuring your iPad remains functional for years.

All the latest iPads support iPadOS 26 and will receive future updates for at least five years. Choosing a newer model ensures longer software support, keeping your device relevant for longer.

Battery Life

Battery performance is an essential consideration, especially if you plan to use your iPad while traveling or for long study/work sessions. Apple rates most iPads for around 10 hours of battery life on typical web browsing and media consumption. However, real-world battery life depends on usage.

  • The iPad (11th Gen) and iPad Air (8th Gen) offer great all-day battery life for casual users.
  • The iPad Pro (M5 chip) consumes more power due to its advanced display and high-performance processor, but it still delivers excellent battery life.
  • The iPad mini (7th Gen) has a smaller battery due to its compact size, but it lasts just as long for regular use.

Portability and Accessories

Portability is an important factor if you plan to carry your iPad regularly. Here’s how each model stacks up in terms of weight and portability:

The iPad mini is the most portable if you prefer a lightweight device. For a larger screen, good portability, and the sleekest design, the iPad Pro 11-inch is a great choice. It’s only 0.21 inches (5.3mm) thin, much less than the mini and Air models!

Additionally, Apple offers several iPad accessories, such as Magic Keyboard, Apple Pencil (2nd gen or Pro), Smart Folio, etc., with unique features. So, you must ensure your chosen iPad is compatible with the accessory you will use the most.

Best iPad accessories:

  • iPad Pro USB-C Hub, 7-in-1 Adapter
  • iPad Docking Station
  • MoKo Sleeve Bag Handle Carrying Case
  • Apple USB-C Digital AV Multiport Adapter

Apple Intelligence

Apple has significantly integrated Apple Intelligence across its iPad lineup, making AI-driven features a key factor in choosing a model. These features can boost productivity, creativity, and automation.

If you want the best AI experience, the iPad Pro with an M5 chip is the top choice, as it can run Apple’s latest AI-powered tools smoothly. The iPad Air with M4 chip is a great mid-range option, while the iPad mini (A17 Pro chip) packs AI into a compact form factor. However, the 11th-generation iPad doesn’t support Apple Intelligence.

Budget

Price is a major deciding factor. Apple’s iPad lineup ranges from budget-friendly to premium options. Pricing also varies based on the storage option you choose. Here’s a breakdown of the starting prices for the iPad lineup:

If you’re on a tight budget, the iPad (11th Gen) is the most cost-effective choice. If you want high performance at a reasonable price, the iPad Air (M4) is a solid middle ground. The iPad Pro is for those who need the absolute best performance and display quality.

Best iPad for Most People: 2025 iPad (A16)

The iPad (11th Gen) is the best choice for most users. It features an 11-inch Liquid Retina display with peak brightness of 500 nits for clear, vibrant visuals. While it might not be the most powerful iPad, the A16 chip still delivers a smooth performance.

The dual mics and landscape stereo speakers ensure good sound quality, making it ideal for everyday tasks like browsing the web, reading, video meetings, consuming content, and light productivity work. With iPadOS 26 support, it’s a budget-friendly yet capable option.

The back features a 12MP Wide camera with 4K video recording and Smart HDR 4 support. The front has a 12MP Center-Stage camera for clear FaceTime video calls. Moreover, Apple doubled the base storage to 128GB, so you can use the device longer.

Besides, by pairing it up with a Magic Keyboard and Apple Pencil (1st gen), you can quickly take notes and go over some work-related stuff. The only downside is that this iPad’s battery doesn’t last an entire day. Also, while testing, I missed the convenience of Face ID and Apple Intelligence features.

So, at $349, the iPad 11th Gen offers a good balance of performance, affordability, and longevity, making it the most affordable iPad for most people, students, and families.

Best iPad for Creators: 2025 iPad Pro M5

If you are wondering about the best iPad for creators, don’t look further than the iPad Pro M5. This 3nm powerhouse chip, with an integrated Neural Accelerator in the GPU, is designed for demanding AI workflows, filmmaking, video editing, graphic design, and music production.

It delivers around 15% better multi-core CPU performance, up to 4x faster GPU compute, up to 153 GB/s of bandwidth, and 45% stronger graphics than the M4. So, you will get the finest AI image & video generation, video editing experience using Final Cut Pro and AI-infused music production on Logic Cut Pro.

Apple has also included its first custom modem, C1X, offering up to 50% faster data speeds and 30% lower power use for longer battery life. Moreover, it features an Ultra Retina XDR OLED display with peak HDR brightness of 1600 nits for the best visuals. You can opt for the Nano-texture display glass for greater clarity.

What’s more? This iPad Pro is only 5.1mm thick, making it the thinnest Apple product. The pro camera system with LiDAR scanner lets you capture 4K ProRes videos. With its 13-inch screen, latest M5 chip, studio-quality mic, and speakers, Apple Intelligence—combined with Apple Pencil Pro and Magic Keyboard—can easily replace your laptop.

Best iPad for Professionals: 2026 iPad Air M4

Do you need a workhorse with pro-like features at an affordable price? The iPad Air M4 is the best choice. Available in 11-inch and 13-inch models, it features a sleek design with a Liquid Retina display that delivers vibrant visuals.

The M4 chip with 12GB of unified memory ensures smooth multitasking, efficient handling of demanding applications, and support for Apple Intelligence processes. Additionally, it has a 9-core GPU with advanced hardware-accelerated ray tracing capabilities for 3D modeling, making it the best iPad for architects.

The best part is that you can use Apple Pencil Pro on this iPad Air and complete your creative tasks in design apps. Further, if you get the 13-inch variant and pair it up with the Magic Keyboard with a larger trackpad, you might as well get a MacBook Air-like setup!

Best iPad for Students: 2024 iPad mini

If you are looking for the ultimate portable, compact iPad, the iPad mini is your answer. It is designed for students who need a handy, lightweight, and affordable device for schoolwork and entertainment. You will get the crisp Liquid Retina display to watch content or read stuff.

Besides, the camera setup does a decent job of scanning documents and attending video calls. Its powerful A17 Pro Bionic chip ensures smooth performance for studying, note-taking, and creative projects. Basically, it can handle all kinds of day-to-day productivity tasks and offer Apple Intelligence features.

However, this price point does not justify the storage option and battery life. Also, you can’t attach a Keyboard case to this iPad. The iPad mini is a great value-for-money device if you can put aside these minor issues.

When and Where to Buy an iPad in 2026?

Buying an iPad at the right time and from the right place can help you save money and get the best value. You can purchase an iPad from several retailers, both online and in-store. The Apple Store is the most reliable option, offering the latest models, customization, and financing options. Apple also offers trade-in discounts.

Amazon frequently offers competitive pricing, bundle deals, and fast shipping for Prime members. You may also check out Best Buy, which offers student discounts and trade-in options for select models. If you prefer offline purchases, you can go to Walmart or Target. They offer occasional discounts on older models.

You can find great deals during major sales events like Back-to-School Season, Amazon Prime Day, Black Friday & Cyber Monday, and Year-End Holiday Sales. Apple often offers free AirPods or discounts on accessories.

If you’re on a budget, consider buying the iPad Pro M4 or the iPad Air M3 instead of the latest models. They still offer similar performance to the latest models, years of iPadOS 26 support, and lower prices after newer models are released. If you need a cellular iPad, some carriers offer discounts when you bundle it with a phone plan.

I also recommend buying a refurbished model to get some good discounts. Apple Refurbished Store is a great place to find certified refurbished iPads at lower prices with Apple’s warranty and battery replacement.

Pick the Right iPad for You!

Choosing the right iPad in 2026 depends on your needs and budget. No matter which iPad you choose, you’re getting a powerful device with Apple’s latest features that will last for years. So, which iPad model caught your eye? Let me know in the comments below!

  • When is the best time to buy an iPhone?
  • Which MacBook should you buy?
  • iPad Air M4 vs iPad Pro M4: Which One Should You Buy?

mainEntity.name: Can all Apple Watches use Precision Finding for AirTags?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Only Apple Watch Series 9 and later, and Apple Watch Ultra 2 and later models running iOS 26.2.1, can use Precision Finding. Older models may still show the AirTag’s location in the Maps in Find Items app, but won’t provide directional guidance.

mainEntity.name: Do you need an iPhone nearby?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Your Apple Watch must remain paired with an iPhone that is connected to the same Apple ID. The iPhone helps manage the connection to the Find My network.

mainEntity.name: How accurate is Precision Finding on Apple Watch?

acceptedAnswer.text: Precision Finding is extremely accurate when you are close to the AirTag. It can guide you within a few feet of the item using directional arrows, distance tracking, and haptic feedback.

About Ava Biswas

  • Ava is a die-hard Apple aficionado and loves testing the latest tech gadgets.
  • She is always on the lookout for issues Apple users are facing, finds solutions, and crafts troubleshooting guides.
  • Her goal to make tech easy for everyone encouraged her to break down complex concepts into easily digestible content.

Experience

Ava has been employing her professional writing and editing skills for over 4 years at renowned media houses like TechBurner and iGeeksBlog. Using her expertise, she crafts informative and engaging How-To's, troubleshooting guides, product reviews, and editorials. When not typing, you can find her exploring the latest Apple releases or pondering new tech innovations.

title.rendered: iPhone Stuck on Apple Logo? 5 Easy Ways to Fix It

content.rendered:
Seeing your iPhone stuck on the Apple logo can be worrying. The phone turns on, shows the Apple logo, and then just sits there. Instead of loading the Home Screen, the device stops during the boot process. This often occurs after an iOS update, during the restoration of a backup, or during startup.

The good news is that most cases are caused by minor software issues that you can resolve on your own. Below, I have covered the most effective methods, from a simple force restart to deeper recovery methods, to fix this issue.

Table of Contents
  • Quick Checks Before Fixing an iPhone Stuck on the Apple Logo
  • Why Is My iPhone Stuck on the Apple Logo? Common Causes
  • Method 1: Force Restart Your iPhone
  • Method 2: Fix iPhone Stuck on Apple Logo Using Recovery Mode
  • Method 3: Restore Your iPhone With DFU Mode
  • Method 4: Use iOS System Repair Tools to Fix the Apple Logo Issue
  • Method 5: Contact Apple Support for Hardware Problems
  • Quick Comparison of Fixes for iPhone Stuck on Apple Logo
  • How to Prevent Your iPhone From Getting Stuck on the Apple Logo
  • Final Thoughts

Quick Checks Before Fixing an iPhone Stuck on the Apple Logo

Before trying the methods below, make sure the iPhone is actually stuck.

  • Wait about one hour: If you see the Apple logo with a progress bar, the update may still be installing.
  • Keep the iPhone plugged in: Updates and restores require steady power and connection.
  • Check for a boot loop: If the Apple logo appears and disappears repeatedly, the iPhone is restarting during startup. This is called a boot loop and requires troubleshooting.

Why Is My iPhone Stuck on the Apple Logo? Common Causes

Several software or hardware problems can trigger this issue. The most common ones are:

  • Interrupted iOS update: The update was interrupted due to low battery or a network interruption.
  • Corrupted system files: A crash or software bug damaged core iOS components.
  • Jailbreaking or unsupported tools: System modifications can break startup processes.
  • Hardware damage: Battery, logic board, or water damage can stop the device from booting.
  • Corrupted backup restore: Errors during a restore can freeze the device at the Apple logo.

Method 1: Force Restart Your iPhone

Force restarting should be the first method to try if your iPhone is stuck. It hard reboots the device and clears temporary or minor system glitches that may stop iOS from starting. This method is safe and doesn’t delete any of your data.

Here’s how to force restart iPhone 8 and later models:

  1. Press and release the Volume Up button.
  2. Immediately press and quickly release the Volume Down button.
  3. Now press and hold the Side button, and release it when the Apple logo appears.

If the iPhone still shows the Apple logo, move to Recovery Mode.

Method 2: Fix iPhone Stuck on Apple Logo Using Recovery Mode

If a force restart doesn’t work, try Recovery Mode. This allows your computer to repair or reinstall iOS on your iPhone. Recovery Mode can update system files or reinstall iOS if the software becomes corrupted during an update or restore.

First, connect your iPhone to a Mac or Windows PC using a Lightning or USB‑C cable and open Finder or iTunes.

Enter Recovery Mode on iPhone 8 and newer:

  1. Connect the iPhone to your computer.
  2. Press and release the Volume Up button.
  3. Then press and release the Volume Down button.
  4. Now press and hold the Side button.
  5. Keep holding until the Recovery Mode screen appears.
  6. Once your device appears in Finder or iTunes on you mac, you’ll see two options:
    • Update – reinstalls iOS without deleting data.
    • Restore – erases the device and installs a new copy of iOS.

Always try Update first. If it fails, choose Restore.

  • iPhone Not Showing Up in Finder? Here’s How to Fix It
  • iPhone Not Showing in iTunes? Here is How to Fix This Annoying Issue

Method 3: Restore Your iPhone With DFU Mode

If nothing else works, try DFU mode. DFU (Device Firmware Update) is the most advanced restore option available on iPhone. Unlike Recovery Mode, DFU loads the device firmware directly without starting iOS. This allows your computer to reinstall the complete system.

Use DFU only if Recovery Mode fails or your iPhone remains stuck in a boot loop. Keep in mind that this process erases all data on the device.

Steps to enter DFU mode:

  1. Connect the iPhone to your Mac (or PC).
  2. Press and release the Volume Up button, then quickly press the Volume Down button.
  3. Hold the Side button until the screen turns black.
  4. Hold the Side button and Volume Down for about 5 seconds.
  5. Release the Side button while holding the Volume Down button.

If done correctly, Finder or iTunes will detect your iPhone and prompt you to restore or update it.

Click Restore iPhone to reinstall iOS on your device.

Method 4: Use iOS System Repair Tools to Fix the Apple Logo Issue

If Recovery Mode or DFU seems too technical, you can try third-party iOS repair tools. These apps connect your iPhone to a computer, scan it, and attempt to automatically repair damaged iOS system files.

Popular options include Tenorshare, iMyFone Fixppo, and Dr.Fone Repair. They guide you through the process step by step. Most of these tools are paid, and they don’t fix every issue, but they can help when standard recovery methods fail.

Method 5: Contact Apple Support for Hardware Problems

If none of the above methods resolve the stuck logo issue, it might be hardware-related. This can happen if your iPhone was dropped, exposed to water, or if a component such as the battery or logic board is damaged. You might also notice overheating during startup or screen flickering.

In that case, it’s best to contact Apple Support. You can book a Genius Bar appointment, visit an Apple Authorized Service Provider, or use Apple’s mail‑in repair service. Apple technicians can run diagnostics and identify whether any hardware component needs repair or replacement.

Quick Comparison of Fixes for iPhone Stuck on Apple Logo

Here’s a quick comparison of the main fixes so you can understand which method to try first.

How to Prevent Your iPhone From Getting Stuck on the Apple Logo

Once your iPhone is working again, follow these tips to reduce the chances of the issue happening again:

  • Install only stable iOS updates and avoid beta versions.
  • Keep the iPhone connected to Wi‑Fi and power during updates.
  • Make sure the battery is at least 50% before updating.
  • Avoid jailbreak tools or unofficial system modifications.
  • Back up your iPhone regularly using iCloud, Finder, or iTunes.

Final Thoughts

Getting stuck on the Apple logo can make it feel like your iPhone is completely unusable. The device turns on, but it never reaches the Home Screen, leaving you unsure what went wrong. The fixes mentioned above walk you through the most reliable ways to bring your device back to life.

FAQs

How long should the Apple logo stay during an update?

Large updates may take several minutes. If the progress bar hasn’t moved for about one hour, the update may be stuck.

Will a force restart delete my data?

No. A force restart only reboots the device and does not erase your files or settings.

Can full storage cause an iPhone to get stuck on the Apple logo?

Yes. If the device’s storage is completely full, iOS may fail to finish updating or starting. Freeing up space or restoring the device can fix the issue.

blockGraphs.question: How long should the Apple logo stay during an update?
blockGraphs.answer: Large updates may take several minutes. If the progress bar hasn’t moved for about one hour, the update may be stuck.

blockGraphs.question: Will a force restart delete my data?
blockGraphs.answer: No. A force restart only reboots the device and does not erase your files or settings.

blockGraphs.question: Can full storage cause an iPhone to get stuck on the Apple logo?
blockGraphs.answer: Yes. If the device’s storage is completely full, iOS may fail to finish updating or starting. Freeing up space or restoring the device can fix the issue.

title.rendered: Shazam Music Recognition Now Available in ChatGPT

content.rendered:
ChatGPT can now identify songs using Apple’s Shazam music recognition technology, allowing users to detect music directly inside the AI assistant without leaving the app. The integration brings Shazam’s audio recognition system into ChatGPT and returns song results within the conversation.

Shazam now works directly inside ChatGPT

Users can start a prompt with “Shazam” or ask a request such as “Shazam, what is this song?” ChatGPT then opens a “Tap to Shazam” interface that activates the microphone and analyzes the audio using Shazam’s recognition technology.

ChatGPT returns a result card with the song title, artist name, and album artwork. A short preview of the track can be played directly in the chat. The system uses the same Shazam recognition technology available on Apple devices, but the entire process runs inside ChatGPT.

Song recognition works even if the standalone Shazam app is not installed. If the Shazam app is installed, songs identified in ChatGPT are added to the user’s Shazam library.

Setup and availability

The integration must be enabled from ChatGPT’s apps section. Users can open settings, navigate to Apps, and add Shazam. After setup, the feature can be triggered by starting a prompt with “Shazam” or invoking the Shazam tool inside ChatGPT.

The feature is rolling out globally and is available in ChatGPT on iOS, Android, and the web. ChatGPT also supports Apple Music and Spotify integrations, allowing users to generate playlists based on identified songs.

The Shazam integration is rolling out globally starting today and is available across ChatGPT platforms.

Also Read: ChatGPT Begins Showing Ads to Free and Go Tier Users in the U.S.

mainEntity.name: Can all Apple Watches use Precision Finding for AirTags?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Only Apple Watch Series 9 and later, and Apple Watch Ultra 2 and later models running iOS 26.2.1, can use Precision Finding. Older models may still show the AirTag’s location in the Maps in Find Items app, but won’t provide directional guidance.

mainEntity.name: Do you need an iPhone nearby?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Your Apple Watch must remain paired with an iPhone that is connected to the same Apple ID. The iPhone helps manage the connection to the Find My network.

mainEntity.name: How accurate is Precision Finding on Apple Watch?

acceptedAnswer.text: Precision Finding is extremely accurate when you are close to the AirTag. It can guide you within a few feet of the item using directional arrows, distance tracking, and haptic feedback.

acceptedAnswer.text: Large updates may take several minutes. If the progress bar hasn’t moved for about one hour, the update may be stuck.

title.rendered: iOS 26.4 Beta 4 Now Available With New Emoji and Security Enhancements

content.rendered:
Apple has seeded iOS 26.4 beta 4 to developers and public beta testers as the company continues refining the upcoming update before its public release.

Although the latest beta does not introduce major headline features, it brings a few notable changes along with security improvements, new emojis, and refinements to features introduced earlier in the iOS 26.4 beta cycle. Here’s everything new in iOS 26.4 beta 4.

New Emoji Characters

Apple has added a new set of emojis that will arrive with the final iOS 26.4 update. The new characters follow the latest Unicode recommendations and expand the emoji library available on iPhone.

Emoji updates are usually rolled out in .4 releases and become available across Apple platforms once the final release goes live.

New Sleep Metric in the Health App

Apple has added an average bedtime metric in the Sleep section of the Health app. This new data point helps users better understand their sleep habits by showing when they typically go to bed over time. The feature complements Apple’s existing sleep-tracking tools on iPhone and Apple Watch.

RCS Encrypted Messaging

Apple has removed the RCS end-to-end encryption testing that appeared in the first three betas of iOS 26.4. The feature was originally being tested as part of Apple’s efforts to improve security for messages exchanged between iPhone and Android users via RCS.

However, Apple has already confirmed that end-to-end encryption for RCS will not launch with iOS 26.4. Instead, the company plans to introduce the feature in a future software update.

Reduce Bright Effects

In iOS 26.4 beta 4, Apple has renamed the existing “Reduce Highlighting Effects” Accessibility setting to “Reduce Bright Effects.” The functionality remains the same, but Apple has updated the name and description to better explain what the setting does.

Bug Fixes and Stability Improvements

As expected for a later beta release, iOS 26.4 beta 4 also includes several bug fixes and performance improvements to stabilize the update before the public rollout.

Public Rollout Expected Soon

With the fourth beta now available, Apple is likely nearing the end of the iOS 26.4 testing cycle. The company typically releases a Release Candidate build shortly after the final developer beta, followed by the public rollout.

If Apple follows its usual schedule, iOS 26.4 could be released to all users in the coming weeks once testing is complete.

Share your thoughts on the latest iOS 26.4 beta changes in the comments below.

mainEntity.name: Can all Apple Watches use Precision Finding for AirTags?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Only Apple Watch Series 9 and later, and Apple Watch Ultra 2 and later models running iOS 26.2.1, can use Precision Finding. Older models may still show the AirTag’s location in the Maps in Find Items app, but won’t provide directional guidance.

mainEntity.name: Do you need an iPhone nearby?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Your Apple Watch must remain paired with an iPhone that is connected to the same Apple ID. The iPhone helps manage the connection to the Find My network.

mainEntity.name: How accurate is Precision Finding on Apple Watch?

acceptedAnswer.text: Precision Finding is extremely accurate when you are close to the AirTag. It can guide you within a few feet of the item using directional arrows, distance tracking, and haptic feedback.

acceptedAnswer.text: No. A force restart only reboots the device and does not erase your files or settings.

About Vikhyat Rishi

  • Vikhyat has over five years of experience writing consumer tech content.
  • During his association with Smartprix and Beebom, Vikhyat has tested, tested, and reviewed numerous gadgets, including but not limited to smartphones, TVs, and more.
  • His passion for technology and Apple products led him to iGeeksBlog, where he specializes in writing How-to and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple enthusiasts.

Experience

Vikhyat embarked on his journey in consumer technology writing in 2019, driven by his passion for technology. He has sharpened his skills through associations with Smartprix and Beebom, where he extensively tested and reviewed various gadgets, focusing mainly on smartphones. Currently, Vikhyat specializes in crafting How-to and troubleshooting guides for the Apple ecosystem at iGeeksBlog. When not typing away on his MacBook Air, he loves exploring the real world.

title.rendered: Best MacBook to Buy in 2026: Prices & Buying Guide

content.rendered:
If you’re planning to buy a MacBook in 2026, choosing the right model can be confusing. Apple now offers several options, including the MacBook Neo, MacBook Air, and MacBook Pro with different screen sizes, Apple Silicon chips, storage options, and price points. But not every model is the right choice for every user.

Whether you’re a student, developer, content creator, or business user, the best MacBook for you depends on your performance needs, budget, and how you plan to use it. In this buying guide for 2026, we’ll compare the MacBooks available right now, explain which chip and configuration you should choose, and help you decide exactly which MacBook you should buy.

Table of Contents
  • Overview of MacBook Models in 2026
    • Current MacBook Lineup (2026)
    • Upcoming MacBooks:
  • Who Should Buy Which MacBook
  • Key Factors to Consider Before Buying a MacBook
    • 1. Performance
    • 2. Storage (SSD)
    • 2. Display
    • 3. macOS & Software Support
    • 4. Battery Life
    • 5. Ports & Connectivity
  • Best MacBook for Students & Casual Users: 13-inch MacBook Neo
  • Best MacBook for Most People: 13-inch MacBook Air M5
  • Best MacBook for Business Users and Creative Professionals: 14-inch MacBook Pro M5 Pro
  • Best MacBook for Power Users and High-end Creators: 16-inch MacBook Pro M5 Max
  • When and Where to Buy a MacBook in 2026
  • Final Thoughts: Buy the Right MacBook for You

Overview of MacBook Models in 2026

Apple currently sells three main lines of MacBooks: MacBook Air, MacBook Pro, and MacBook Neo.

The MacBook Air offers a balance of performance, portability, and battery life at a great value, while the MacBook Pro delivers high-end performance and advanced features for professionals.

On the other hand, Apple launched MacBook Neo for students and casual users. It focuses on basic tasks like browsing, streaming, and document work while keeping the price lower than Air and Pro models.

Note Apple discontinued the M4, M3, and M2 MacBook Air models after launching the M5 MacBook Air in March 2026. The 14-inch MacBook Pro M4 was also replaced by the M5 MacBook Pro in October 2025.

Current MacBook Lineup (2026)

Upcoming MacBooks:

  • MacBook Pro M6 expected in late 2026
  • MacBook Ultra with OLED and Touchscreen display is rumoured to arrive in late 2026.

Who Should Buy Which MacBook

  • Best MacBook for students, casual & budget users: 13-inch MacBook Neo
  • Best MacBook for most people for office work and everyday productivity: 13-inch MacBook Air M5
  • Best MacBook for business users, developers and creative professionals: 14-inch MacBook Pro M5 Pro
  • Best MacBook for power users, high-end creators, and engineers: 16-inch MacBook Pro M5 Max

Key Factors to Consider Before Buying a MacBook

Here are all the factors to consider when choosing the best MacBook for your needs.

1. Performance

Apple silicon chips are known for exceptional speed and power efficiency. The right one for you depends on your needs and budget.

  • A18 Pro: First time an iPhone chip is used in a MacBook. It’s power-efficient and perfect for students and everyday users.
  • M5: The base chip of the M5 family with up to 3.5x faster AI performance, better graphics, and faster SSDs than the last generation.
  • M5 Pro: A balanced powerhouse for business professionals and developers who run demanding apps.
  • M5 Max: The most powerful option, ideal for 4K/8K video editors, 3D artists, and graphic designers.

Choosing the right unified memory (RAM) is just as important as it affects how smoothly your MacBook handles multitasking and heavy apps. Avoid underpowering your workflow, but don’t overspend on specs you’ll never use.

Read more: A18 Pro vs M1: How Apple’s iPhone Chip Compares to the First Mac Silicon

2. Storage (SSD)

MacBooks use fast SSD storage, which affects how many files, apps, and projects you can store.

256GB–512GB is fine for everyday users, whereas 1TB or more is better for creators working with large files, such as videos or design projects.

You can also use external SSDs if you need extra space.

2. Display

Every MacBook features Apple’s premium Retina display, but the Pro models offer additional advantages, including ProMotion (120Hz adaptive refresh rate) and higher brightness levels.

Screen sizes range from 13-inch to 16-inch, so choose based on your usage—portability or workspace comfort.

3. macOS & Software Support

Apple’s macOS 26 Tahoe runs on all current MacBooks. Based on Apple’s update history, expect at least 6–7 years of software support for any M-series model.

If you want the longest longevity, pick a MacBook with the newest chip.

4. Battery Life

All latest MacBooks are battery-efficient, but the Pro models tend to last slightly longer due to larger batteries. The Air lineup trades a bit of endurance for portability, making it perfect for travelers and students.

5. Ports & Connectivity

The MacBook Neo keeps things minimal in terms of connectivity, with two USB-C ports (USB 3 and USB 2) and a 3.5mm jack. Next, the Air model expands the connectivity with a MagSafe charging port, two Thunderbolt/USB 4 ports, and a 3.5mm jack.

The MacBook Pro adds an HDMI port, an SD card slot, and an extra Thunderbolt 4/5 port, giving you greater flexibility for external displays and storage.

Best MacBook for Students & Casual Users: 13-inch MacBook Neo

The latest MacBook Neo is the most affordable MacBook in Apple’s lineup startng at only $599. It’s designed for everyday tasks like browsing, streaming, writing assignments, and attending online classes.

Powered by the A18 Pro chip, the MacBook Neo delivers smooth performance for daily apps while maintaining great battery life. Its 13-inch Liquid Retina display, lightweight design, and reliable macOS experience make it a practical entry point into the Apple ecosystem.

Key highlights

  • A18 Pro chip for fast everyday performance
  • 13-inch Liquid Retina display with sharp visuals
  • Up to 16 hours of battery life for all-day use
  • 256GB base variant with a 512GB option
  • Lightweight and portable for school or travel

Best MacBook for Most People: 13-inch MacBook Air M5

The 13-inch MacBook Air with the M5 chip is the best MacBook for most people in 2026. It offers the perfect balance of performance, portability, and price, making it ideal for students, remote workers, writers, and everyday users.

Powered by Apple’s M5 chip, the laptop delivers faster performance while staying extremely power-efficient. The chip also improves AI processing and multitasking, making everyday tasks feel smooth and responsive. Moreover, Apple’s updated N1 chip offers Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6.

Key Highlights

  • M5 chip with up to a 10-core CPU and dedicated Neural Accelerator
  • 13.6-inch Liquid Retina display with bright, sharp visuals
  • Up to 18 hours of battery life for all-day use
  • 512GB base variant with up to 4TB configuration available
  • Lightweight fanless design, making it silent and easy to carry

If you need a larger display, you can go for the 15-inch MacBook Air, which costs $200 more.

Best MacBook for Business Users and Creative Professionals: 14-inch MacBook Pro M5 Pro

The 14-inch MacBook Pro with the M5 Pro chip is designed for professionals who need serious performance in a portable laptop. It’s a powerful choice for business users, software developers, video editors, and designers who run demanding apps and multitask heavily.

The M5 Pro chip offers the world’s fastest single-core CPU performance, significantly higher GPU performance, and 2x faster SSD than the standard M5, making tasks like compiling code, editing high-resolution videos, or working with large AI models much faster.

Key Highlights

  • M5 Pro chip for high-performance workflows
  • 14-inch Liquid Retina XDR display with HDR and up to 1,600 nits brightness
  • Up to 64GB unified memory with 307GB/s of memory bandwidth for heavy multitasking
  • Base storage option upgraded to 1TB with up to 4TB options
  • Multiple ports, including Thunderbolt, HDMI, SD card slot, and MagSafe
  • Up to 24 hours of battery life for long work sessions

On the other hand, the 16-inch MacBook Pro is a powerful workstation for professionals working in visual media.

Best MacBook for Power Users and High-end Creators: 16-inch MacBook Pro M5 Max

The 16-inch MacBook Pro with the M5 Max chip is Apple’s most powerful laptop in 2026. It’s built for power users, filmmakers, 3D artists, engineers, and AI developers who need extreme performance for demanding workloads.

The M5 Max chip delivers massive GPU power and supports up to 128GB of unified memory, making it ideal for tasks like 3D rendering, machine learning, and editing multiple streams of 4K or 8K video. The chip can include up to a 40-core GPU with Neural Accelerator that significantly boosts graphics and AI performance compared with earlier generations.

Key Highlights

  • M5 Max chip with a powerful CPU and up to a 40-core GPU for heavy workloads
  • 16.2-inch Liquid Retina XDR display with ProMotion for professional-grade visuals
  • Up to 128GB unified memory with 614GB/s of memory bandwidth for advanced creative and AI workflows
  • 2TB default storage with up to 8TB configuration
  • Multiple pro ports, including Thunderbolt, HDMI, SD card slot, and MagSafe
  • All-day battery life despite the high performance

The larger 16-inch display and bigger battery are ideal for professionals who need maximum power on the go, without switching to a desktop.

When and Where to Buy a MacBook in 2026

The best time to buy a MacBook is when you need it, but timing can help you save.

Look for deals during Black Friday, Cyber Monday, or Back-to-School sales. Students can also claim Apple’s education discount for added savings.

Avoid buying right before major Apple launch events, which usually take place in March and October, to prevent missing out on new models or price drops.

You can buy directly from Apple.com, Amazon, or Best Buy. Refurbished models can also be great deals, but ensure you buy from a trusted source.

Final Thoughts: Buy the Right MacBook for You

That’s everything you need to know about buying a MacBook. Apple has a MacBook for every kind of user, from students and professionals to creatives and business executives.

Choosing the right one depends on how you plan to use it. Take your time, match your workflow to the specs, and you’ll have a MacBook that lasts you years without compromise.

  • Best Accessories for MacBook Air
  • Mac keyboard shortcuts for Apple Notes
  • Best Mac apps to download (Free and paid)

mainEntity.name: Do you need an iPhone nearby?
