title.rendered: Mac Processor History: How Apple Transformed Computing

content.rendered:
When you think of a Mac today, you probably imagine a fast, powerful machine powered by Apple’s latest M5 chip. But Macs weren’t always this advanced. Their journey began in the 1980s with the Motorola 68K series—a much simpler processor. Over the years, Apple transitioned to PowerPC, then Intel, and finally, its own Apple Silicon chips.

In this article, we’ll explore how Mac processors have evolved over time. You’ll see how each new chip improved speed, graphics, and memory, shaping the powerful Macs we use today.

Table of Contents
  • 2020–Present: Apple Silicon
    • M5 Chip Family: M5, M5 Pro, and M5 Max
    • M4 Chip family: M4, M4 Pro, and M4 Max
    • M3 Chip Family: M3, M3 Pro, M3 Max, and M3 Ultra
    • M2 Chip Family: M2, M2 Pro, M2 Max, and M2 Ultra
    • M1 Chip family: M1, M1 Pro, M1 Max, and M1 Ultra
  • 2006-2020: Intel x86
  • 1994-2005: Power PC
  • 1984-1995: Motorola 68 K

2020–Present: Apple Silicon

On June 22, 2020, Apple CEO Tim Cook announced a two-year transition plan to move from Intel processors to Apple Silicon. The goal was to create an all-Apple ecosystem by replacing Intel’s x86-64 architecture with Apple’s native ARM64-based chips.

Staying true to its timeline, Apple introduced its first Apple-designed chip, M1, in November 2020. This was followed by more powerful M1 variants in 2021. Apple then launched the M2, M3, M4, and M5 chipsets, further pushing the boundaries of performance.

Here’s a detailed table outlining the evolution of Mac processors, from the latest Apple M4 Max back to the M1:

M5 Chip Family: M5, M5 Pro, and M5 Max

M5 (October 2025)

The M5 is the base chip in the M5 family and is created using  TSMC’s third-generation 3-nanometer process for mainstream laptops and tablets. It’s the first Apple Silicon chip to feature a dedicated Neural Engine in the GPU core, focusing on AI-driven tasks.

The chip features a 10-core CPU made up of 6 performance and 4 efficiency cores and up to a 10-core GPU, which provides solid graphics performance for tasks like photo editing and light 3D work. You can also configure it up to 32 GB of unified memory.

In Geekbench Single-Core scores, the M5 base model outperforms the whole M4 series and has the highest scores of any Apple silicon chip. Overall, it delivers a strong balance of performance, efficiency, and affordability for most users.

M5 Pro (March 2026)

The M5 Pro is designed for professionals who need more processing power than the base M5. Apple has designed a new Fusion Architecture specifically for AI tasks in this chip. It includes an 18-core CPU (6 super and 12 performance cores), offering 30% faster processing of intensive workloads. Apple has stated it as “the world’s fastest single-core performance.”

The GPU can scale up to around 20 cores with a dedicated Neural Accelerator in each core, delivering much stronger graphics performance. One of the major improvements in the M5 Pro is higher memory bandwidth up to 307GBps and up to 64 GB of unified memory, enabling large projects and datasets to run smoothly without slowdowns.

M5 Max (March 2026)

The M5 Max sits at the top of the M5 chip lineup and is built for users who need maximum performance. It is targeted at professionals working in fields such as 3D rendering, medical imaging, advanced video production, machine learning, and large-scale creative projects.

This chip features the same high-performance CPU architecture as the M5 Pro but dramatically expands the GPU capabilities. The GPU can scale up to 40 cores, making it one of the most powerful graphics systems available in a laptop.

The M5 Max also offers up to 614GBps memory bandwidth and supports up to 128 GB of unified memory. So, it can run large professional projects efficiently without relying heavily on external storage.

M4 Chip family: M4, M4 Pro, and M4 Max

Apple’s M4 chip family represents the latest advancements in silicon technology, delivering enhanced performance and efficiency across various devices. Each chip—M4, M4 Pro, and M4 Max—is designed to meet different user needs.

M4 (May 2024)

The standard M4 chip is built using second-generation 3-nanometer technology, enhancing power efficiency and performance. It features a 10-core CPU with four performance cores and six efficiency cores, delivering up to 1.8 times faster performance than the M1 chip.

The 10-core GPU provides graphics performance up to twice as fast as the M1, making tasks like photo editing and gaming smoother. The 16-core Neural Engine, capable of performing up to 38 trillion operations per second, significantly boosts AI-related tasks and features like Apple Intelligence.

M4 Pro (October 2024)

The M4 Pro chip is designed for users with more demanding workflows. It boasts a 14-core CPU, comprising ten performance cores and four efficiency cores, offering up to 1.9 times faster performance than the M1 Pro.

The GPU includes up to 20 cores, providing graphics performance twice that of the standard M4. This makes it ideal for professionals engaged in tasks like app development, video editing, and complex simulations.

M4 Max (October 2024)

The M4 Max chip is the most powerful in the M4 family, targeting users requiring extreme performance. It features a 14-core CPU with ten performance cores and four efficiency cores, similar to the M4 Pro.

However, its GPU scales up to 32 cores, delivering exceptional graphics capabilities suitable for high-end tasks such as 3D rendering and large-scale data processing. The M4 Max also supports higher unified memory bandwidth, enhancing data-intensive operations.

All M4 chips support advanced features like hardware-accelerated ray tracing and mesh shading, enhancing graphics rendering and gaming experiences. They also enable Thunderbolt 5 connectivity, offering faster data transfer speeds and improved peripheral support.

M3 Chip Family: M3, M3 Pro, M3 Max, and M3 Ultra

Apple’s M3 chipset family includes four powerful processors: M3, M3 Pro, M3 Max, and M3 Ultra. Each is designed to meet different performance needs, from everyday tasks to demanding professional workloads.​

M3 (October 2023)

The M3 chip is built using advanced 3-nanometer technology, making it faster and more efficient. It features an 8-core CPU with four performance cores and four efficiency cores, delivering up to 30% faster performance than the M1.

The 10-core GPU provides enhanced graphics performance, making tasks like photo editing and gaming smoother. The 16-core Neural Engine, capable of performing up to 15.8 trillion operations per second, significantly boosts AI-related tasks.

M3 Pro (October 2023)

The M3 Pro chip is designed for users with more demanding workflows. It boasts a 12-core CPU, comprising six performance cores and six efficiency cores, offering up to 40% faster performance than the M1 Pro.

The GPU features up to 18 cores, delivering graphics performance ideal for professionals in video editing, programming, and other demanding tasks. Apple has also integrated 37 billion transistors to enhance the overall performance of Mac machines.

M3 Max (October 2023)

The M3 Max chip is one of the most powerful in the M3 family, targeting users requiring extreme performance. It features a 14-core CPU with ten performance cores and four efficiency cores, similar to the M3 Pro.

However, its GPU scales up to 38 cores, delivering exceptional graphics capabilities suitable for high-end tasks such as 3D rendering and large-scale data processing. The M3 Max also has 92 billion transistors to enhance data-intensive operations.

M3 Ultra (March 2025)

The M3 Ultra chip is Apple’s most powerful processor to date. It features a 32-core CPU with 24 performance cores and eight efficiency cores, delivering up to 1.8 times the performance of the M1 Ultra.

Its GPU includes up to 80 cores, providing up to 2.6 times faster graphics performance than the M1 Ultra. The M3 Ultra also supports up to 512GB of unified memory—the highest ever in a personal computer—making it ideal for tasks like visual effects and AI development.

M2 Chip Family: M2, M2 Pro, M2 Max, and M2 Ultra

M2 (June 2022)

The M2 processor in the MacBook houses an 8-core CPU with a configuration of 4 performance cores and 4 efficiency cores. Apple claims that M2’s CPU gives twice the performance of the latest 10-core PC laptop processor.   

In addition, the M2 processor offers unparalleled work performance with an 8—or 10-core GPU, 16-core neural engine, and 100GBps bandwidth. M2 chips have different RAM variations: 8GB, 16GB, and 24 GB. 

M2 Pro (January 2023) 

M2 Pro has a robust 10-core or 12-core CPU, including 6 or 8 performance and 2 efficiency cores. Like the M1 Pro, the M2 Pro has an inbuilt media engine that accelerates H.264, HEVC, and ProRes video encoding and decoding. Besides, the chip provides improved power efficiency when playing 4K and 8K ProRes streams thanks to the 16- or 19-core GPU.

Further, the M2 Pro has a 16-core neural engine, 200 GBps memory bandwidth, and 16 GB or 32 GB RAM variants. Apple claimed the M2 Pro offered exceptional image processing capabilities. However, it is only equipped with a MacBook Pro to handle its high efficiency.   

M2 Max (January 2023) 

M2 Max added another layer of efficiency to the Apple Silicon range. Its core specifications included a 12-core CPU with 8 performance and 4 efficiency cores. Like its predecessor, the M2 Max comes with two ProRes and video-encoding engines.   

Regarding graphics, it supports a 30- or 38-core GPU to give you the most detailed output. While the GPU support is better than M1 Max, the 16-core neural engine remains the same for both variants. In addition, Apple introduced the chip in 3 RAM variants- 32 GB, 64 GB, and 96 GB.   

Moreover, Apple asserted that the M2 Max was 30% better than the M1 version when using color grading in DaVinci Resolve. It also offers 400 GB of memory bandwidth, ensuring quick processing.   

M2 Ultra (June 2023) 

At the recent WWDC 2023, Apple launched its most efficient iteration of the Apple Silicon series: M2 Ultra. It offers the power of two M2 Max chips interwoven using the robust UltraFusion architecture. Regarding specifications, M2 Ultra features a 24-core CPU and a maximum of 76-core GPU support.

It also carries 134 billion transistors, up to 192GB of unified memory, and an impressive 800 GB of memory bandwidth. You can experience this beast in the latest Mac Studio and Mac Pro. According to Apple, Mac Studio with M2 Ultra is 3x faster than its earlier version.

Besides, it can run 22 streams of 8K ProRes video together. The M2 Ultra chip enables the Mac Pro to deliver 3D simulations and video transcoding up to 3x faster. Moreover, the processor can simultaneously consume 24 inputs from 4K cameras and encode them to ProRes. 

M1 Chip family: M1, M1 Pro, M1 Max, and M1 Ultra

M1 (November 2020)

The M1 processor was Apple’s first venture into chip design for the Mac. Indeed, it was a big blow for Intel! Regarding specs, M1 chips offer an 8-core CPU with 4 performance and 4 efficiency cores and a 7- or 8-core GPU support.

Besides, the 16-core Neural Engine embedded in the M1 series accelerates and optimizes machine learning operations on Mac. In addition, the chip offered 68.25 GB of memory bandwidth. However, it only supported two RAM variations—8GB and 16GB. The small storage capacity didn’t go down well with many Mac users.  

M1 Pro (October 2021)

Next in line in the M1 series was M1 Pro. This chipset supported 8-or-10-core CPUs, configured as 6 or 8 performance and 2 efficiency cores. Besides, Apple included a 14-or-16-core GPU, which is 2x faster than M1. Also, the new GPU was up to 7x more quickly than the integrated graphics on the 8-core laptop chip.

Besides, it featured a ProRes accelerator in the media engine for faster video processing. Its memory bandwidth of up to 200 GB is nearly 3x better than the M1. This time, Apple expanded its storage capacity with M2, introducing 16GB and 32GB chips. 

M1 Max (October 2021)

The M1 Max and M1 Pro chips were launched together. They had a 10-core CPU with 8 performance and 2 efficiency cores, a 24- or 32-core GPU, and a 16-core Neural Engine. The graphics performance of the 32GB GPU is up to 4x faster than that of the M1 chip.   

Its two ProRes accelerators can deliver up to 2x faster video encoding than M1 Pro. Moreover, the processor offers up to 400 GB of memory bandwidth, two times more than the M1 Pro and 6x improved than the M1. Besides, the 64GB RAM adds some extra credit points.   

Apple introduced the M1 Max chip only for the MacBook Pro and Mac Studio.   

M1 Ultra (March 2022)

The M1 Ultra was launched as a standard option for the Mac Studio. This powerful processor has UltraFusion architecture connecting the two M1 Max chips. It houses a 20-core CPU with 16 performance and 4 efficiency cores. For graphics, Apple added a massive 48- or 64-core GPU support.

So, you get improved latency, reduced bandwidth, and better power consumption. Furthermore, the chip has up to 128GB of unified memory built, offering twice the media engine performance of the M1 Max.   

2006-2020: Intel x86

At WWDC 2005, Apple announced its transition to Intel chips, and the first Intel Macs were announced in early 2006. These included an iMac and the MacBook Pro, which boasted almost four-fold enhanced performance from their predecessors. 

Further, from Mac OS X 10.4.4, Apple included an advanced emulation technology called Rosetta. It helped maintain software compatibility between generations. Soon, Apple introduced programs with universal binaries that could run on both PowerPC and Intel Macs.

As the transition to x86 eventually came a full circle, Rosetta was removed from Mac OS X 10.7 Lion going forward. So far, about 80 Mac models have featured Intel CPUs. This changed with the introduction of ARM-based Macs.

1994-2005: Power PC

In the late 1980s, new trends began taking over the computing industry, overshadowing the legacy CPU architectures. Apple partnered with IBM and Motorola to design a common CPU platform that could rival the “Wintel” (Microsoft-Intel) domination. 

The Power Macintosh 6100 used the PowerPC architecture, following which around 87 different Mac models were launched. Clock speeds increased from 60 MHz to 2.7 GHz, which was remarkable for that era. The final Apple PowerPC model was released in November 2005. 

1984-1995: Motorola 68 K 

The 1984 Apple Macintosh computer had an 8 MHz Motorola 68000 CPU. While in development, an early Mac prototype used an 8/16-bit Motorola 6809 CPU. But after a designer noticed the impressive graphics routines that were being created for the 68000-based Apple Lisa, the more expensive 16/32-bit 68000 was chosen. 

While the Apple Lisa used only a 5 MHz 68000, the new Mac prototype could run at 8 MHz. This appealed to Steve Jobs, who was eager to upstage the Lisa team. 

Over the following decade, every Macintosh used successors of the 68000, including the pure 32-bit 68020, 68030, and 68040 chips. These got faster and more complex over time. Overall, at least 72 different Macs used 68k CPUs, the last of which was the PowerBook 190 in 1995. 

The best is yet to come! 

The history of Apple processors beautifully captures the tech giant’s true ideology. The Mac has witnessed everything from laptop size to its architecture. I hope you enjoyed reading this article as much as we enjoyed traveling the Mac timeline while penning it.

Please share your reviews in the comments section. Till then, enjoy reading.

title.rendered: First MacBook Neo Benchmarks Reveal Power of Apple’s A18 Pro Chip

content.rendered:
The first benchmark results for Apple’s newly announced MacBook Neo are now online, offering an early look at how the A18 Pro performs inside a Mac.

The results show that Apple’s iPhone chip delivers performance that is surprisingly competitive with entry-level Mac processors. The MacBook Neo scored 3,461 in single-core tests and 8,668 in multi-core tests, numbers that closely match those of the iPhone 16 Pro.

The reason is simple. Both devices run the same A18 Pro chip, though the MacBook Neo ships with a slightly reduced GPU configuration.

GPU Difference Explains Metal Score Gap

Graphics performance is where the first difference appears. The MacBook Neo recorded a Metal score of 31,286, slightly lower than the iPhone 16 Pro’s 32,575. This gap exists because the MacBook Neo includes one fewer GPU core.

Aside from graphics, the CPU results are almost identical between the two devices.

How the MacBook Neo Stacks Up Against Other Apple Devices

Looking beyond the iPhone comparison, the MacBook Neo delivers performance that lands in an interesting spot within Apple’s lineup.

The numbers reveal a shift. While the Neo cannot match the multi-core power of newer M-series chips, its single-core performance is far ahead of the original M1 MacBook Air.

Related: MacBook Neo vs MacBook Air: Full Comparison (Specs, Price, Features)

Why Strong Single-Core Performance Matters?

Single-core speed still plays a major role in many everyday computing tasks.

Activities such as browsing websites, opening apps, writing documents, and watching videos often depend more on single-thread performance than raw multi-core throughput. In these areas, the A18 Pro performs extremely well.

That makes the MacBook Neo well-suited for students, casual users, and people who mainly use a laptop for productivity and media.

Apple is Targeting a Different Segment

Apple is not positioning the MacBook Neo against its own Mac lineup. Instead, the company is aiming directly at budget laptops powered by Windows or ChromeOS.

Apple claims the A18 Pro is:

  • up to 50% faster in everyday tasks than the best-selling PC with an Intel Core Ultra 5 processor
  • up to three times faster for on-device AI workloads
  • up to twice as fast for photo editing

This positioning explains the Neo’s aggressive starting price.

Related: A18 Pro vs M1: How Apple’s iPhone Chip Compares to the First Mac Silicon

Price and Availability

The MacBook Neo starts at $599, making it the most affordable Mac Apple currently sells.

Preorders are already open, and the laptop will begin shipping on March 11.

More benchmark entries will likely appear over the coming days, which should give a clearer picture of real-world performance. Early results already confirm one thing. Apple’s iPhone chips are now powerful enough to comfortably power entry-level Macs.

Would you buy the MacBook Neo based on these benchmarks? Tell us in the comments below.

To get the most out of your MacBook Neo, the right accessories are essential. They can boost productivity, expand connectivity, and keep your mac protected.

title.rendered: A18 Pro vs M1: How Apple’s iPhone Chip Compares to the First Mac Silicon

content.rendered:
Apple transitioned away from Intel to Apple Silicon in 2020 with the introduction of the M1 chip. Devices powered by the M1 chip, such as the MacBook Air and Mac mini, set a new benchmark for performance and efficiency.

Fast forward four years, Apple introduced the A18 Pro chip in the iPhone 16 Pro, which has now appeared in the company’s new entry-level laptop, the MacBook Neo.

This development raises an interesting question. How does the A18 Pro compare with the M1 chip that started Apple’s Mac silicon journey? Let’s take a closer look at how these two Apple chips compare.

Table of Contents
  • Apple A18 Pro vs M1: Quick Comparison
  • Apple A18 Pro vs M1: CPU Performance
    • Single-Core Performance
    • Multi-Core Performance
  • Apple A18 Pro vs M1: GPU Performance
  • A18 Pro vs M1: AI and Neural Engine
  • A18 Pro vs M1: Efficiency and Power Consumption
  • A18 Pro vs M1: Which Chip Is Better?
  • Why is Apple Using the A18 Pro in the MacBook Neo?
  • Final Verdict

Apple A18 Pro vs M1: Quick Comparison

Apple A18 Pro vs M1: CPU Performance

Starting with the CPU, the Apple M1 chip is built on TSMC’s 5nm process, while the newer A18 Pro uses a more advanced 3nm manufacturing node. The smaller process helps the A18 Pro achieve higher efficiency and improved performance.

Single-Core Performance

The A18 Pro delivers noticeably stronger single-core performance in my tests.

It scored 1840 in Geekbench 6’s single-core test, compared to the M1’s 1463. This means the newer chip performs better in tasks that rely on a single CPU core.

Single-core performance affects everyday tasks such as:

  • launching apps
  • browsing the web
  • scrolling through interfaces
  • opening documents

This is also one reason Apple can use the A18 Pro in the MacBook Neo, where fast everyday responsiveness matters more than sustained heavy workloads.

Multi-Core Performance

Multi-core results tell a slightly different story. The M1 scored 4616, while the A18 Pro scored 4362 in Geekbench 6 multi-core tests.

This advantage comes from the M1’s 8-core CPU design, which includes four performance cores and four efficiency cores. Macs also operate within higher power limits, allowing them to maintain performance under sustained workloads.

For tasks such as video rendering, code compilation, and large multitasking workloads, the M1 still has a slight advantage.

Apple A18 Pro vs M1: GPU Performance

Moving to GPU performance, Apple has significantly improved graphics capabilities in its recent A-series chips. The 6-core GPU on the A18 Pro chip introduces architectural improvements and higher efficiency compared to earlier Apple silicon.

In my Geekbench GPU tests, the MacBook Air (M1, 2020) powered by the Apple M1 chip scored 21,417 in the Metal benchmark. Meanwhile, the iPhone 16 Pro with the A18 Pro achieved a Metal score of 18,352.

While the M1 still delivers stronger raw GPU performance in this test, the difference is surprisingly small, given that the A18 Pro is designed for a smartphone. Apple’s improvements in GPU architecture and efficiency allow the chip to deliver competitive graphics performance despite operating within a much smaller power envelope.

In real-world usage, both chips can comfortably handle tasks such as photo editing, casual gaming, UI rendering, and graphics-heavy apps.

This level of graphics performance also explains why Apple can power devices like the MacBook Neo with the A18 Pro while still delivering smooth everyday graphics performance.

A18 Pro vs M1: AI and Neural Engine

Both chips feature Apple’s 16-core Neural Engine, but the newer A18 Pro chip brings noticeable improvements in machine learning capabilities and efficiency. Apple continues to refine its AI hardware each generation to support more advanced on-device intelligence.

The Neural Engine on the A18 Pro delivers up to 35 trillion operations per second (TOPS), enabling faster processing for tasks such as image recognition, natural language processing, and AI-powered photo editing. In comparison, the Apple M1 chip offers around 11 TOPS of AI compute, which was impressive at the time of its launch but now falls behind newer Apple silicon.

The stronger AI engine allows devices like the iPhone 16 Pro to run advanced machine learning workloads directly on the device. These include features such as real-time image processing, voice recognition, and on-device AI tasks.

With Apple increasingly focusing on AI-powered features across its platforms, the improved Neural Engine in the A18 Pro also helps devices like the MacBook Neo handle modern AI workloads more efficiently while maintaining excellent power efficiency.

A18 Pro vs M1: Efficiency and Power Consumption

The A18 Pro chip is built on TSMC’s 3nm process, which allows it to deliver higher performance while consuming less power. In comparison, the Apple M1 chip is manufactured using TSMC’s 5nm process. While the M1 was highly efficient when it launched in 2020, the smaller 3nm node gives the A18 Pro a clear performance advantage per watt.

Another key factor is the target device class. The A18 Pro is designed primarily for smartphones like the iPhone 16 Pro, where power efficiency is critical to maintain long battery life in a compact form factor. The M1, on the other hand, powers larger devices such as the MacBook Air (M1, 2020), which can operate within higher power limits for sustained workloads.

Despite these differences, both chips are extremely efficient compared to traditional laptop processors. The improved efficiency of the A18 Pro is also what allows Apple to power devices like the MacBook Neo with a smartphone-class processor while still delivering strong everyday performance and excellent battery life.

A18 Pro vs M1: Which Chip Is Better?

Neither chip outshines the other, as both are impressive and excel in different areas.

A18 Pro advantages

  • Faster single-core performance
  • Competitive GPU performance in some workloads
  • Newer architecture
  • Better power efficiency

M1 advantages

  • Better sustained performance
  • More CPU cores
  • Designed specifically for Mac workloads
  • Higher multi-core performance

Why is Apple Using the A18 Pro in the MacBook Neo?

Apple’s decision to power the MacBook Neo with the A18 Pro chip highlights how far its mobile silicon has evolved in recent years. Even though the A18 Pro was originally designed for smartphones like the iPhone 16 Pro, its performance is now strong enough to compete with early Apple Silicon Mac chips, such as the Apple M1. As our benchmarks show, the A18 Pro delivers competitive CPU and GPU performance while maintaining excellent efficiency.

At the same time, the A18 Pro’s 3nm architecture enables outstanding power efficiency. This allows the MacBook Neo to deliver long battery life while maintaining a thin and fanless design.

Ultimately, using the A18 Pro helps Apple position the MacBook Neo as a more affordable entry-level Mac while still delivering modern performance and efficiency. For most everyday users, the chip provides more than enough power to run macOS smoothly.

Final Verdict

The A18 Pro and M1 represent two different phases of Apple Silicon evolution. The M1 marked the beginning of the Mac transition away from Intel and delivered incredible performance for laptops in 2020. But Apple’s mobile chips have improved rapidly since then.

Today, the A18 Pro matches or even exceeds the M1 in several areas, including single-core performance and AI processing. With Apple now using the chip in devices like the MacBook Neo, it’s clear that the line between iPhone chips and Mac processors is becoming thinner every year.

What are your thoughts on Apple using the A18 Pro in MacBook Neo? Join the discussion in the comments.

title.rendered: MacBook Neo vs MacBook Air: Full Comparison (Specs, Price, Features)

content.rendered:
Apple’s Mac lineup now includes a wider range of laptops than ever before. At the entry level is the new MacBook Neo, a budget-friendly option to make the Mac experience more accessible. Above it sits the MacBook Air, which is the mainstream ultraportable Mac for the masses.

The MacBook Neo focuses on the basic everyday tasks like web browsing, streaming videos, writing documents, and light productivity work. However, the MacBook Air is built for users who need more performance, better hardware features, and stronger multitasking capabilities. As the Neo model is priced way lower than the Air, there are many tradeoffs.

In this guide, I’ll share a detailed comparison of MacBook Neo vs. MacBook Air, including their specs, design, performance, battery life, and price, so you can decide which is better for everyday use.

Table of Contents
  • MacBook Neo vs MacBook Air: Quick Comparison
  • Design and Build Quality
  • Performance: A-Series vs M-Series Chips
  • Display Comparison
  • RAM and Storage Options
  • Ports and Connectivity
  • Keyboard, Touch ID, Camera, Mic, and Speaker Specs
  • Battery Life Compared
  • MacBook Neo vs. MacBook Air: Price and Value
    • Final Verdict: Which MacBook Should You Buy?

MacBook Neo vs MacBook Air: Quick Comparison

The table makes the positioning clear: MacBook Neo is the budget Mac, while MacBook Air is the more powerful everyday laptop. Now let’s break it down further!

Design and Build Quality

In terms of overall look, both laptops follow Apple’s familiar minimalist design. They use aluminum bodies, slim profiles, and large trackpads.

The MacBook Neo looks similar to the Air but includes a few cost-saving changes. It has thicker display bezels and a slightly thicker body, although the overall size and weight are close to the Air. The laptop weighs about 2.7 pounds, which is nearly identical to the MacBook Air.

Apple also introduced more playful colors for the Neo, including Silver, Blush, Citrus, and Indigo, which gives it a slightly more casual and student-friendly look. These colors extend to its Magic keyboard as opposed to the black backlit keyboard on the Air.

The MacBook Air, by contrast, is built as a premium ultraportable device. It features thinner edges, a more refined chassis, and a slightly larger display in a similarly compact body. Apple positions it as the laptop most people should buy if they want a balance of portability and performance.

Overall, the build quality of both machines is excellent, but the MacBook Air feels more premium and refined, while the Neo focuses on affordability.

Performance: A-Series vs M-Series Chips

The biggest technical difference between the two laptops is the processor.

The MacBook Neo uses Apple’s A18 Pro chip, which originally debuted in the iPhone lineup. This chip includes:

  • 6-core CPU with 2 performance cores and 4 efficiency cores
  • 5-core GPU
  • 16-core Neural Engine
  • 60GB/s memory bandwidth

While that may sound impressive, the A-series chip is designed primarily for iPhones, not full computers. As a result, its performance is suitable for everyday tasks but not heavy workloads. Some of the tasks that the Neo can handle well include web surfing, streaming videos, writing documents, online classes, and basic photo editing.

On the other hand, the MacBook Air runs Apple’s M-series chips such as the M5. These chips are designed specifically for Macs and deliver much higher performance.

For example, the M5 chip can include:

  • 10-core CPU with 4 super cores and 6 efficiency cores
  • 8-core or higher GPU with integrated Neural Accelerators
  • 16-core Neural Engine
  • 153GB/s memory bandwidth

Therefore, it’s 20% faster for single-core tasks and 80% faster for multi-core tasks than A18 Pro chips. This makes the MacBook Air significantly better for tasks like video editing, programming, graphic design, large spreadsheets, and heavy multitasking.

So, in terms of performance comparison, the MacBook Neo is good for light computing, while the MacBook Air is built for demanding workloads.

Display Comparison

Both laptops use Apple’s Liquid Retina display technology, but there are still several differences.

The MacBook Neo features a 13-inch Liquid Retina display with a resolution of 2408 × 1506 pixels and brightness of about 500 nits. However, it lacks several advanced display technologies, including True Tone support and P3 wide color gamut.

Instead, it uses a more basic sRGB color range, which means colors are slightly less vibrant than on higher-end Macs. Also, the display bezels are slightly thicker for cost-cutting.

The MacBook Air offers a more advanced display. It’s available in larger 13.6-inch and 15-inch screen, 2560 by 1664 pixel resolution, wider P3 color support, and additional technologies that improve color accuracy and viewing comfort.

For everyday use, like watching videos or browsing the web, both screens look great. But for photo editing, design work, or color-sensitive tasks, the MacBook Air clearly has the better display.

RAM and Storage Options

Memory and storage options are another major difference between the two laptops.

The MacBook Neo is limited to 8GB of unified memory, and there is no option to upgrade it. Storage starts at 256GB and can be upgraded to 512GB. For light users, this configuration is usually enough. But for people who run many apps at once or work with large files, the limitation can become noticeable.

But the MacBook Air is far more flexible. It starts with 16GB of RAM and offers upgrade options such as 24GB or 32GB RAM, and has storage options up to 4TB. This means the MacBook Air can handle much heavier workloads and remain useful for many years.

Ports and Connectivity

Connectivity is another area where the MacBook Air offers more advanced features.

The MacBook Neo includes two USB-C ports and a 3.5mm headphone jack. However, these USB-C ports are limited in speed. One supports USB 3 (10 Gb/s) and the other only USB 2 speeds (480 Mb/s). It also supports only one external 4K display at 60Hz.

On the other hand, the MacBook Air offers a much stronger port setup:

  • Two Thunderbolt 4 ports (40 Gb/s speeds)
  • MagSafe 3 charging port
  • 3.5mm headphone jack

It can also support multiple external displays, including up to two 6K displays, depending on the configuration. So, in everyday use, the MacBook Air works much better with docks, external monitors, and professional accessories.

Keyboard, Touch ID, Camera, Mic, and Speaker Specs

The MacBook Neo includes Apple’s Magic Keyboard and a large trackpad, but there are a few compromises to keep the price low.

For example:

  • The keyboard does not include backlighting.
  • The base model only has a Lock key. For Touch ID, you need the 512GB model.
  • It uses a standard mechanical multi-touch trackpad instead of the Force Touch trackpad found in other Macs.

The Neo still includes useful hardware such as a 1080p FaceTime HD camera, dual microphones with voice isolation and directional beamforming, and dual stereo speakers with Spatial Audio and Dolby Atmos support. So, you can enjoy music and video streaming.

In contrast, the MacBook Air offers a more premium input and audio experience. It includes:

  • Backlit Magic Keyboard
  • Touch ID on all models
  • Force Touch trackpad
  • 12MP Center Stage camera with Desk View support
  • LED webcam indicator light and Ambient light sensor
  • Improved four speakers and a three-mic array

These upgrades make the MacBook Air better for video calls, music, movies, and long typing sessions.

Battery Life Compared

Battery life takes a major place in the MacBook Neo vs. MacBook Air comparison. Thanks to Apple’s efficient silicon chips, both laptops can survive day-to-day usage.

The MacBook Neo includes a 36.5-watt-hour lithium-ion battery and can last up to:

  • 11 hours of web browsing
  • 16 hours of video playback

The MacBook Air has a larger 53.8-watt-hour lithium-polymer battery and can reach:

  • 15 hours of web browsing
  • 18 hours of video playback

Both laptops easily last a full day for typical use, but the MacBook Air usually lasts slightly longer.

Another difference is charging. The Neo charges through 20W USB-C only, while the Air includes MagSafe charging, which frees up ports and disconnects safely if the cable is pulled. It supports a 40W Dynamic Power Adapter with a 60W Max.

MacBook Neo vs. MacBook Air: Price and Value

The biggest difference between the two laptops is price.

The MacBook Neo starts at $599, making it Apple’s cheapest MacBook ever, whereas the MacBook Air starts at $1,099, which is about $500 more expensive.

That price difference reflects the hardware improvements in the Air, including:

  • Faster M-series processor
  • Better display
  • More RAM and storage options
  • Thunderbolt connectivity
  • MagSafe charging
  • Longer battery life

So the choice really comes down to budget vs performance.

If you only need a simple laptop for everyday computing, the MacBook Neo offers excellent value. But if you want a more powerful laptop that will last longer and handle demanding tasks, the MacBook Air is worth the extra cost.

Final Verdict: Which MacBook Should You Buy?

The MacBook Neo and MacBook Air are designed for very different types of users.

The MacBook Neo is best for students, casual users, families buying multiple laptops, first-time Mac buyers, and basic everyday computing. It delivers the core macOS experience at the lowest price Apple has ever offered. The MacBook Air is better for professionals, creators and developers, heavy multitaskers, and users who want a long-term laptop.

If your needs are simple and budget matters most, the MacBook Neo is a great entry point into the Mac ecosystem. But if you want stronger performance, better features, and a laptop that can handle more demanding tasks over time, the MacBook Air remains the better overall MacBook for most people.

What’s your thoughts? Let us know in the comments below!

  • iPad Pro M5 vs. Samsung Tab S11 Ultra

title.rendered: 8 Must-Have Accessories for Your New iPhone 17e

content.rendered:
That first week with a new iPhone is always the same. You handle it like it is made of glass, avoid pockets with keys, and plug it in before the battery dips too low.

Accessories are how you keep that “new phone care” going later without thinking about it.

A solid case and screen protector take the hit from daily scuffs. And now that the iPhone 17e supports MagSafe, you can set up cleaner charging at your desk or carry a magnetic power bank when you are out. There are also MagSafe add-ons that make quick errands simpler.

Here are eight essential accessories for your new iPhone 17e that protect and enhance it without adding bulk.

Table of Contents
  • 1. Apple iPhone 17e Silicone Case
  • 2. Spigen Ultra Hybrid (MagFit) Case
  • 3. IMBZBK Screen Protector
  • 4. Apple FineWoven MagSafe Wallet
  • 5. Anker 3-in-1 Cube Charging Station
  • 6. Anker Nano MagSafe Power Bank
  • 7. LISEN Magnetic Car Mount
  • 8. AirPods Pro 3
  • The Quick Setup that Covers Everything

1. Apple iPhone 17e Silicone Case

If you want a slim case that protects the phone without making it bulky, Apple’s official silicone case is usually the easiest pick. It’s a thin silicone shell with a soft-touch exterior (Apple says it’s made from 45% recycled silicone), and the inside has a microfiber lining so the back of the phone rests against fabric instead of plastic.

There is a small raised lip around the screen and camera module, so they are not the first things to touch a table. The case also has Apple’s built-in magnet ring, which keeps MagSafe wallets and battery packs properly aligned and allows charging on MagSafe or Qi2 pads without removing the case. It also works with crossbody straps if you prefer carrying your phone hands-free. Color options include Black, Anchor Blue, Bright Guava, Light Moss, Soft Pink, and Vanilla.

At $49, it is more expensive than many third-party cases, but it remains a dependable choice if you want a slim case that fits well, protects the phone, and works cleanly with MagSafe accessories.

Check out on Apple Store

2. Spigen Ultra Hybrid (MagFit) Case

If you like seeing the actual color and design of your iPhone 17e, a clear case usually makes more sense than covering it up. Spigen’s Ultra Hybrid (MagFit) does exactly that with a transparent polycarbonate back and flexible TPU edges that wrap around the frame.

That combination is the main reason people pick this case. The rigid back keeps the case clear and scratch-resistant, while the softer TPU bumper helps absorb impacts if the phone falls. Spigen also adds its Air Cushion pockets in the corners, which are designed to take most of the shock during drops.

There is a raised edge around the screen and camera so they do not rest directly on a table. The case also includes a magnet ring for MagSafe accessories and wireless charging. Spigen’s magnets are known to be quite strong, which helps wallets, stands, and battery packs stay firmly attached.

It is priced at $44.99 in the US and comes in several clear variants like Clear White, Clear Graphite, Clear Gold, Clear Deep Blue, and Clear Orange. If you want protection but still want the phone’s design to remain visible, this is one of the more practical clear cases to consider.

Check out on Amazon

3. IMBZBK Screen Protector

A screen protector is one of the easiest ways to avoid scratches on the iPhone 17e’s display, and IMBZBK’s tempered glass pack is a practical option because it usually comes with three protectors in the box. It typically sells for around $12–$15 on Amazon, which means you have spares if the first one cracks or the installation goes wrong.

The kit includes an alignment frame, cleaning wipes, and dust stickers. The frame sits on the phone and helps place the glass in the correct position, which makes installation much easier compared to applying a protector by hand.

The glass is thin and transparent, with an oleophobic coating to reduce fingerprints and smudges. It is also cut to be case-friendly, so most cases will not lift the edges. Some versions of the pack also include camera lens protectors, and there are variants such as clear, matte anti-glare, and privacy glass, depending on what you prefer.

Check out on Amazon

4. Apple FineWoven MagSafe Wallet

If you prefer carrying just a few cards instead of a full wallet, Apple’s FineWoven MagSafe Wallet attaches magnetically to the back of the iPhone 17e or a MagSafe case and holds up to three cards, such as a credit card, ID, or transit card.

It’s made from Apple’s FineWoven microtwill material using 100% recycled content and has a soft, suede-like texture. The wallet also includes RFID shielding to help protect cards from unwanted scanning.

One useful feature is Find My support. Once paired with your iPhone, it can show the wallet’s last known location in the Find My app if it gets separated from the phone.

It costs $59 in the US and comes in colors like Black, Navy, Fox Orange, Moss, and Pacific Blue. If you already use MagSafe accessories, it’s a clean way to carry a couple of cards without bringing a separate wallet.

Check out on Amazon

5. Anker 3-in-1 Cube Charging Station

If you charge multiple Apple devices every day, the Anker 3-in-1 Cube keeps everything in one place. It’s a compact charging station that powers an iPhone 17e, Apple Watch, and AirPods at the same time.

The cube unfolds to reveal a magnetic Qi2 charging pad for the iPhone, a pop-up Apple Watch charger, and a flat spot for AirPods with wireless charging. The iPhone pad delivers up to 15W wireless charging and snaps into alignment magnetically.

When folded, the whole charger turns into a small cube measuring about 3.3 inches on each side, which makes it easy to pack for travel or keep on a desk without taking up much space. The box also includes a 40W USB-C charger and cable.

It sells for $129.99 in the US. If you use an iPhone, Apple Watch, and AirPods together, this kind of charger simplifies the setup by replacing three separate charging cables with one compact dock.

Check out on Anker Store

6. Anker Nano MagSafe Power Bank

If you want a backup battery without carrying cables, Anker’s Nano magnetic power bank snaps onto the back of the iPhone 17e and starts charging wirelessly.

It has a 5,000mAh capacity, which is usually enough to give the phone roughly one extra charge depending on usage. It supports up to 15W wireless charging and also includes a USB-C port for pass-through charging, so you can recharge the power bank while it is attached to the phone.

The main advantage is its size. At about half an inch thick, it stays fairly pocket-friendly compared to larger magnetic batteries. Some versions also include a small kickstand for propping the phone up while watching videos.

It typically sells for around $40–$50 in the US and comes in colors like Black, White, and Blue.

Check out Best Buy

7. LISEN Magnetic Car Mount

If you use your iPhone 17e for navigation in the car, a MagSafe-style mount is much easier than the old clamp-style holders. The LISEN magnetic car mount lets you snap your phone onto it and remove it in a second.

It uses strong magnets to hold the phone in place, and the base attaches to the dashboard using a 3M adhesive pad. Once installed, the arm and mount can be adjusted to position the phone at a comfortable viewing angle while driving.

The mount works with the iPhone 17e and other MagSafe-compatible cases. It does not include wireless charging, but the magnetic attachment keeps the phone stable even on rough roads.

Depending on the model, it usually sells for around $17–$30 in the US. If you regularly use Apple Maps, Google Maps, or Waze while driving, a magnetic mount like this makes the iPhone much easier and safer to use in the car.

Check out on Amazon

8. AirPods Pro 3

If you are using an iPhone 17e, AirPods Pro 3 work seamlessly with it. Pairing is instant through Apple’s automatic setup, and features like Spatial Audio, head tracking, and device switching work smoothly across Apple devices.

They use Apple’s H3 chip for Active Noise Cancellation, Adaptive Audio, and Transparency mode. The charging case also includes a U2 chip, which enables Precision Finding in the Find My app when used with newer iPhones like the 17e.

The earbuds include custom drivers for clear sound, touch controls with swipe gestures for volume, and silicone tips in multiple sizes for a secure fit. Both the earbuds and the case are rated IP54 for dust, sweat, and water resistance.

Battery life is rated at up to 6 hours with noise cancellation on, and up to 30 hours with the charging case. The case supports USB-C and wireless charging. AirPods Pro 3 are priced at $249 in the US.

Check out on Amazon

The Quick Setup that Covers Everything

If you want the simple, balanced kit:

  • Choose a case: Apple Silicone for the cleanest fit, or Spigen Ultra Hybrid to show off the phone
  • Add protection: IMBZBK screen protector
  • Use MagSafe well: FineWoven wallet for daily carry, 3-in-1 Cube for home charging, Nano power bank for travel

This is the combination that keeps the iPhone 17e protected, makes charging easier, and adds just enough utility to feel like an upgrade without turning your phone into a project.

In case you missed

  • Buy iPhone 17e Now or Wait for iPhone 18
  • iPhone 17e vs iPhone 17

title.rendered: How to Turn Off Location on Snapchat (Step-by-Step Guide)

content.rendered:
Snapchat’s Snap Map is a fun way to discover what’s happening around you, letting you explore snaps and stories from friends and nearby users. However, it also shows your location to friends on the map when location sharing is enabled, which might raise privacy concerns for some users.

To help protect users’ privacy, Snapchat lets you share your location with specific friends, hide it from certain people, turn it off for everyone using Ghost Mode, or completely disable location access in your phone’s settings.

Keep reading to learn how Snapchat location sharing works and how to turn off location on Snapchat.

Table of Contents
  • What Is Snapchat Location Sharing and How Does It Work?
  • How to Turn Off Location on Snapchat
    • Method 1: Turn On Ghost Mode on Snapchat
    • Method 2: Hide Your Snapchat Location From Specific Friends
    • Method 3: Disable Snapchat Location Access From Phone Settings
    • On iPhone:
    • On Android:
  • Does Snapchat Track Your Location When the App Is Closed?
  • What Happens When You Turn Off Location on Snapchat?
  • Summing Up

What Is Snapchat Location Sharing and How Does It Work?

Location sharing is a Snap Map feature that updates your approximate location on the map every time you open the Snapchat app. It helps users discover nearby snaps, view local stories, and know where friends are when they are active on the app.

All your friends on the platform can view your location on the live map through your Bitmoji. The visibility of your location depends on your privacy settings, which let you share it with all friends, selected friends, or no one using Ghost Mode.

If you don’t use Snapchat for a while, your location automatically disappears from Snap Map. Additionally, you can completely disable location access at any time in your phone’s settings for added privacy.

How to Turn Off Location on Snapchat

As previously mentioned, Snapchat lets you turn off your location on the Snap Map entirely or for selected friends, while still keeping location access enabled for other purposes.

Method 1: Turn On Ghost Mode on Snapchat

Ghost Mode on Snapchat lets you turn off your location on the Snap Map while still allowing you to view friends’ locations when they have location sharing enabled.

  1. Open the Snapchat app and tap the Snap Map (Location Pin) icon in the bottom-left corner.
  2. Tap the Settings icon.
  3. Toggle on Ghost Mode.
  4. Select the Until Turned Off option in the pop-up menu that appears.

Method 2: Hide Your Snapchat Location From Specific Friends

If you don’t want to disappear completely but prefer to hide your location from certain friends, Snapchat lets you customize who can see your location.

  1. Tap the Settings icon on the Snap Map tab.
  2. Tap My Friends, Except under the Who Can See My Location section.
  3. Select the accounts you want to turn off location sharing for, then tap Save.

Method 3: Disable Snapchat Location Access From Phone Settings

While Ghost Mode hides your location from friends, Snapchat can still access location data internally. To completely turn off location on Snapchat, you need to change your device’s permissions.

On iPhone:

  1. Go to Settings → Apps → Snapchat.
  2. Tap Location.
  3. Select Never under Allow Location Access.

Also Read: How to Change Your Location on an iPhone

On Android:

  1. Go to Settings → Apps → Snapchat.
  2. Tap Permissions → Location.
  3. Select Don’t Allow under Location access for this app.

Does Snapchat Track Your Location When the App Is Closed?

No, Snapchat does not actively update or share your live location while the app is closed. Your location on Snap Map updates only when you open and use Snapchat.

When you leave the app, your last known location may remain visible to friends for a few hours. After a period of inactivity, Snapchat automatically removes your location from the map until you reopen the app.

Keep in mind that this also depends on your phone’s location permissions. If location access is set to Always, Snapchat can access location data at the system level, but your Snap Map location still refreshes primarily when the app is in use. Setting location permission to Never completely prevents Snapchat from accessing your location.

What Happens When You Turn Off Location on Snapchat?

When location sharing is disabled:

  • Your Bitmoji disappears from Snap Map.
  • Friends cannot track your real-time location.
  • You can still view the map and stories.
  • Snapchat stops updating your visible location on the Snap Map.

Summing Up

Turning off your location on Snapchat takes only a few seconds once you know where to look. Enabling Ghost Mode instantly hides your location, while device-level permissions let you control how much data Snapchat can access.

Have more Snapchat privacy questions? Ask them in the comments section.

FAQs

Will friends know if I turn off my location?

No. Snapchat does not notify others when you enable Ghost Mode or turn off location sharing with them.

Can Snapchat still see my location?

Yes, unless you revoke location permissions from your phone settings.

title.rendered: Garden Horizons Codes (April 2026)

content.rendered:
Update: Verified the latest Garden Horizons Codes on April 10, 2026

Starting in Garden Horizons can feel slow. You begin with a small patch of land, basic seeds, and limited Shillings. Every upgrade takes time, and early progress depends heavily on how efficiently you plant, harvest, and reinvest. That is exactly why redeeming the latest Garden Horizons codes matters.

These codes give you free Shillings, seed packs, sprinklers, and exclusive items that would normally require hours of farming. If you want faster expansion, stronger mutation chances, and better automation early on, claim them immediately.

All Working Garden Horizons Codes

  • MONSTER: 5 Royal Seed Packs (NEW)

Developers can disable codes at any time, so redeem them as soon as possible.

For more in-game rewards, be sure to check our Anime Eternal codes, SpongeBob Tower Defense codes, and Solo Hunters codes guides.

Expired Garden Horizons Codes

358, ADMIN, CONSOLE, DAWN, DAWNFRUIT, GIFT, RELEASE, THANKYOU

How to Redeem Garden Horizons Codes

Redeeming codes is straightforward:

  1. Launch Garden Horizons in Roblox.
  2. Click the Cogwheel icon in the top-left corner.
  3. Scroll down to the Codes text box in Settings.
  4. Enter a working code exactly as shown.
  5. Press the arrow button to claim rewards.

Rewards are applied instantly if the code is valid.

Why a Code Might Not Work

If a code fails, check the following:

  • The code was typed incorrectly. They are case-sensitive.
  • The code has expired.
  • You already redeemed it.
  • You are not part of the required Roblox group for group-exclusive codes such as DAWN and DAWNFRUIT.
  • Roblox servers have been unstable following a recent update.

For group-exclusive rewards, join the official Dawn Digital Roblox group, restart the game, and try again.

Check the All Roblox Game Codes Master List to find working codes for every game.

When New Garden Horizons Codes Are Released

New codes usually drop during:

  • Major updates and patches
  • Player milestone celebrations
  • Seasonal events

Developers typically share them through their official Discord server and X account, especially in the dedicated codes channel. You can also bookmark this page. We will update the codes as soon as new codes drop. 

Fastest Way to Earn More Shillings

Codes provide a boost, but efficient gameplay sustains growth. Check the quest billboard near the shops for daily and weekly tasks. These quests reward bonus Shillings and seed packs and are often more profitable than passive harvesting alone.

Reinvest profits into higher-tier seeds instead of repeatedly planting low-value crops. Focus on crops with strong mutation potential and scale automation with sprinklers to increase output per cycle.

What Garden Horizons Is About

Garden Horizons is a Roblox farming simulator developed by Dawn Digital. You start with a basic plot, buy seeds from the shop, plant them, wait for them to grow, and sell your harvest for Shillings. Those Shillings fund better seeds, sprinklers, decorations, and land expansions.

The depth comes from its mutation system and weather mechanics. Certain crops can mutate into rarer, higher-value variants. Completing your flora diary, finishing quests, and climbing leaderboards adds long-term goals beyond simple harvesting. While it takes inspiration from Grow a Garden, it builds on the formula with more layered progression and competitive elements.

Why Codes Are Important Early Game

Progress in the first few hours is limited by how quickly you can generate Shillings. Basic seeds provide modest returns, and growth cycles take time. Codes eliminate that bottleneck.

With rewards like 50k Shillings or premium seed packs, you can:

  • Purchase high-value seeds immediately
  • Unlock sprinklers to automate crop growth
  • Increase chances of valuable mutations
  • Expand your land sooner
  • Invest in stronger long-term setups

Instead of grinding low-tier crops, you move directly into mid-game progression.

Do Garden Horizons Codes Expire?

title.rendered: macOS Will Flag the Slower USB-C Port on MacBook Neo

content.rendered:
Apple has equipped the new MacBook Neo with two USB-C ports, but they are not identical in terms of functionality and performance. While the laptop may appear to have symmetrical connectivity, the capabilities of each port differ significantly.

The USB-C port on the left side supports USB 3 speeds up to 10 Gbps. This faster port is designed for high-bandwidth tasks, such as connecting external SSDs, docks, and displays.

Meanwhile, the USB-C port located closer to the trackpad, is limited to USB 2 speeds of just 480 Mbps. This makes it suitable for charging and basic accessories, but it cannot handle more demanding connections.

External Display Works Only Through One Port

Due to this hardware limitation, Apple confirms that external display connectivity is supported only through the left USB-C port. Attempting to connect a monitor through the slower right side port will not work for display output.

Apple says the MacBook Neo supports one external display with up to 4K resolution at 60 Hz, allowing users to extend their workspace to a larger screen.

macOS Warns If You Use the Wrong Port

Since the ports are not labeled on the MacBook Neo, users could easily plug an external display into the wrong port.

However, according to Daring Fireball’s John Gruber, macOS helps reduce this confusion. If you connect a display to the slower USB 2 port, the system shows a notification informing you that the display must be connected to the other port.

Pricing and Availability

The MacBook Neo is currently available to pre-order in the United States, starting at $599. Apple also offers a $499 price for college students, making it the most affordable MacBook in the company’s lineup.

The laptop is scheduled to officially launch on March 11.

Would this USB-C port limitation affect your buying decision? Let us know in the comments.

excerpt.rendered: The MacBook Neo includes two USB-C ports with different capabilities. The left port supports faster speeds and external displays, while the right port is limited to USB 2 speeds for charging and basic accessories.

title.rendered: Apple Launched Studio Display and Studio Display XDR: Full Specs, Features, and Price

content.rendered:
Apple has officially unveiled two new professional monitors: Studio Display (2026) and the all-new Studio Display XDR. Designed for creators, developers, and professional workflows, these displays bring major upgrades such as Thunderbolt 5 connectivity, 5K resolution, improved camera and audio systems, mini-LED backlighting and up to 120Hz refresh rates.

Both displays were announced alongside Apple’s latest Mac hardware and are available for pre-order starting March 4, 2026, with shipping beginning March 11. In this article, we’ll break down the features, specifications, and pricing of both Studio Display and Studio Display XDR, and explain who should buy each monitor.

2026 Apple Studio Display: The Ideal Companion for Your Mac Setup

The 2026 Apple Studio Display is an updated version of Apple’s popular 27-inch monitor introduced in 2022. The new model keeps the 5K Retina display but adds better connectivity, improved audio, and smarter video-calling capabilities.

Key Features

  • 27-inch 5K Retina Display with over 14 million pixels
  • A19 chip
  • 600 nits brightness
  • P3 wide color support with 1 billion colors
  • True Tone technology
  • 12MP Center Stage camera with Desk View
  • Three studio-quality microphones
  • Six-speaker audio system (four force-cancelling woofers + two high-performance tweeters) with Spatial Audio
  • Two Thunderbolt 5 ports + two USB-C ports
  • Up to 96W power delivery for MacBooks

The display retains its 60Hz refresh rate, making it ideal for content creators, designers, developers, and general professional workflows rather than high-refresh gaming. If you are using a Mac Studio or a MacBook Pro, this monitor is ideal for everyday usage.

Apple also offers an optional nano-texture glass version to reduce glare in bright work environments.

Apple Studio Display XDR: World’s Best Pro Display

The Studio Display XDR is Apple’s new flagship professional monitor, replacing the Pro Display XDR. It is designed for high-end workflows such as HDR filmmaking, color grading, VFX, diagnostic radiology, and 3D rendering.

Highlights

  • 27-inch Retina XDR 5K display with 5120 × 2880 resolution
  • Mini-LED backlight with over 2,304 local dimming zones
  • A19 Pro chip
  • 1000 nits of SDR brightness and peak HDR brightness up to 2,000 nits
  • 1,000,000:1 contrast ratio
  • 120Hz refresh rate with Adaptive Sync between 47Hz to 120Hz
  • P3 and Adobe RGB color support
  • New DICOM medical imaging presets
  • 12MP Center Stage camera with Desk View
  • Six-speaker Spatial Audio system and studio-quality three-microphone array
  • Thunderbolt 5 connectivity
  • Up to 140W power delivery

The mini-LED technology dramatically improves contrast, HDR performance, and brightness, making it ideal for color-critical professional work.

Overall, the Studio Display XDR is built for demanding workflows like HDR video editing, film production, color grading, and professional photography. Its 120Hz adaptive refresh rate also ensures smoother visuals and animation editing.

Studio Display vs Studio Display XDR

Both monitor have 80% recycled glass in their standard glass models, which is described as “Apple First” in the official press release.

In short:

Studio Display is best for everyday creative workflows.

Studio Display XDR is built for high-end professional production environments.

Connectivity and Ecosystem Integration

Both displays include Thunderbolt 5 connectivity, offering significantly faster data transfer and improved power delivery compared with earlier Thunderbolt versions.

Other connectivity features include daisy-chaining multiple displays, USB-C accessory support, and MacBook charging via a single cable. This makes them ideal companions for devices like the latest Mac Studio, MacBook Pro, Mac mini, and iPad Pro.

However, you can’t use Studio Display XDR with Intel Macs and its limited to 60Hz when connected to M1, M1 Pro, M1 Max, M1 Ultra, M2, and M3 Mac and iPad models.

Price and Availability

Apple has positioned the monitors for different professional segments:

  • Studio Display starts at $1,599
  • Studio Display XDR starts at $3,299

Both monitors are open for pre-order on March 4, 2026, and will be available starting March 11, 2026.

Bottom Line

Apple’s new Studio Display and Studio Display XDR significantly upgrade its monitor lineup.

The standard Studio Display remains a premium 5K monitor for Mac users, while the Studio Display XDR takes it to the extreme with its use of mini-LED HDR, 120Hz refresh rates, and extreme peak brightness.

For professionals in creative industries, these displays aim to deliver studio-grade visuals, powerful connectivity, and deep integration with the Apple ecosystem.

title.rendered: iPad Air M4 vs iPad Pro M4: Which One Should You Buy?

content.rendered:
With the launch of the new iPad Air powered by M4, the traditional gap between Air and Pro has almost disappeared. You now get desktop-class performance, modern connectivity, Apple Pencil Pro support, and large display options without paying Pro-level pricing. At the same time, the iPad Pro M4 remains Apple’s most advanced tablet, thanks to its OLED display, thinner chassis, and higher-tier chip configuration.

So the real question is not which one is better. Which one makes more sense for you?

Let’s break it down properly.

Table of Contents
  • Quick Comparison: iPad Air M4 vs iPad Pro M4
  • Design and Build Quality
  • Display: The Real Differentiator
  • Performance and Real World Usage
  • Cameras, Audio, and Extras
  • Accessories and Ecosystem
  • Battery Life
  • Price and Value
  • Final Verdict: Which One Should You Buy?

Quick Comparison: iPad Air M4 vs iPad Pro M4

Design and Build Quality

At first glance, both iPads look nearly identical. Apple’s flat-edge aluminum design, slim bezels, and USB-C port give them the same modern aesthetic.

The iPad Pro M4 is technically thinner and slightly more refined in engineering. It also uses Face ID for authentication, which feels seamless when unlocking in landscape mode. The iPad Air M4 sticks with Touch ID integrated into the top button. It works reliably, though it does not feel as fluid as Face ID.

In daily use, both feel premium. The difference here is not dramatic enough to influence most buyers. If biometrics matter to you, the Pro has the advantage. Otherwise, this category is largely even.

Display: The Real Differentiator

This is where things begin to separate. The iPad Air M4 uses a Liquid Retina LCD panel with excellent color accuracy, strong brightness, and sharp resolution. For note-taking, streaming, browsing, and even photo editing, it performs exceptionally well.

The iPad Pro M4, however, features Apple’s Ultra Retina XDR OLED display with a ProMotion 120Hz refresh rate. Blacks are deeper. Contrast is stronger, HDR content looks dramatically better, and scrolling feels smoother due to adaptive refresh.

  • If you work with HDR video, color grading, or high-frame-rate creative workflows, the Pro display is objectively superior.
  • If you consume content, edit casually, and use productivity apps, the Air’s display is more than sufficient.

For most users, this will not be a compromise. For visual professionals, it absolutely matters.

Performance and Real World Usage

Both iPads run on Apple’s M4 chip, but they are not identical internally. The iPad Pro M4 features a higher-tier configuration designed for sustained peak workloads. It handles prolonged exports, 3D rendering, and heavy multi-layer editing more efficiently.

The iPad Air M4 uses a slightly tuned configuration of the same architecture. In practical terms, this means the Air remains extremely fast for multitasking, video editing, graphic design, and even demanding AI tasks.

Here’s the honest truth.

Most users will not notice the difference. You only begin to see separation during long, resource-intensive workflows. If your work involves large video timelines, advanced 3D modeling, or heavy professional rendering, the Pro justifies itself. Otherwise, the Air delivers flagship-level performance at a lower cost.

Cameras, Audio, and Extras

The iPad Pro keeps an edge with its advanced camera system and LiDAR scanner, which benefits augmented reality workflows and certain professional environments.

The iPad Air M4 handles video calls, content capture, and casual photography perfectly well, thanks to Center Stage.

So, unless your workflow depends on AR scanning or high-end production setups, this difference will not affect you.

Accessories and Ecosystem

Both iPads support Apple Pencil Pro and the Magic Keyboard. You are not restricted with the Air. You still get full iPadOS multitasking, external display support, and Apple Intelligence features.

Apple has not artificially limited the Air’s ecosystem compatibility. That makes it far more compelling this generation.

Battery Life

In typical use, both iPads last all day. Browsing, note-taking, streaming, and productivity tasks show similar endurance. The Pro may perform better during prolonged heavy workloads, but for normal use, battery life is comparable.

Price and Value

This is where the buying decision becomes clearer. The iPad Pro M4 commands a premium price because it offers the best display, stronger sustained performance, and high-end engineering. The iPad Air M4 delivers 80 to 90 percent of that experience at a significantly lower entry cost.

If you are not monetizing your iPad through professional creative work, the Pro can feel excessive. For students, writers, designers, developers, and most professionals, the Air hits the sweet spot in terms of value.

Final Verdict: Which One Should You Buy?

The iPad Pro M4 is the most advanced iPad Apple makes. Its OLED display, 120Hz ProMotion, and higher-tier M4 configuration make it the right tool for professionals working with HDR video, complex 3D projects, or sustained heavy exports.

But here is the reality.

The iPad Air M4 is no longer a “lite” alternative. It delivers serious desktop-class performance, supports the same core accessories, and handles nearly every productivity and creative task most users throw at it.
If your work doesn’t consistently push hardware limits, the Air gives you better value without sacrificing the experience that actually matters day-to-day.

The Pro is the best. The Air is the smarter buy for most people.

Are you leaning toward the iPad Air M4 or going all in on the Pro? Drop your pick in the comments and tell us how you plan to use it.

title.rendered: Apple Pre‑Orders Now Live for iPhone 17e, MacBook Neo, M5 Macs and More

content.rendered:
Apple has opened global pre‑orders for several newly announced devices, including the iPhone 17e, MacBook Neo, updated MacBook Pro and MacBook Air models with M5 chips, the M4 iPad Air, and two new Studio displays. Orders began at 6:15 a.m. Pacific Time, with shipments and in‑store availability scheduled for March 11.

The devices are available through Apple’s online store worldwide, with pre‑order availability starting simultaneously across regions. Because of that synchronized launch, the exact start time varies by location.

Apple Products Available for Pre‑Order

The current pre‑order wave includes updates across Apple’s phone, tablet, computer, and display lineup.

The newly introduced MacBook Neo is a 13‑inch laptop powered by Apple’s A18 Pro chip. The device starts at $599 and is offered in four colors: Silver, Indigo, Blush, and Citrus.

Apple’s iPhone 17e starts at $599 with 256GB of base storage. The device includes Apple’s A19 chip, MagSafe support, and the company’s C1X modem for cellular connectivity.

Apple is also accepting orders for its new MacBook Pro lineup with M5 Pro and M5 Max chips. Pricing begins at $2,199 for the 14‑inch model and $2,699 for the 16‑inch model, with the update also bringing faster SSD storage.

The MacBook Air has also been refreshed with the M5 chip and now starts at $1,099 with 512GB of base storage.

In tablets, Apple is offering the updated iPad Air with an M4 chip, 12GB of RAM, and Wi‑Fi 7 support, starting at $599.

Apple’s new external displays are also included in the pre‑order window. The Studio Display starts at $1,599 with standard glass or $1,899 with nano‑texture glass, while the Studio Display XDR starts at $3,299 with standard glass or $3,599 with nano‑texture glass. Both displays include Thunderbolt 5 connectivity, with the XDR model adding mini‑LED technology and a 120Hz refresh rate.

Global Pre‑Order Start Times

Apple opens pre-orders worldwide at the same moment. Orders begin at 6:15 a.m. Pacific Time, which converts to different local times depending on region.

How to Place an Apple Pre‑Order

Apple allows customers to place pre‑orders through its website or the Apple Store app. The typical ordering process follows these steps:

  1. Visit the Apple Online Store or open the Apple Store app on iPhone or iPad.
  2. Choose the product and select configuration options such as storage capacity or color.
  3. Sign in using an Apple ID.
  4. Confirm payment method and shipping or pickup details.

Apple notes that the Apple Store app can process orders faster during periods of heavy traffic, which can matter in the first hours of availability when popular configurations may sell out.

Release Date

All of the newly announced devices are scheduled to launch on March 11. Customers who complete pre‑orders early typically receive shipments on release day, while later orders may ship later depending on demand and configuration availability.

title.rendered: MacBook Neo: Price, Specs, Features, and Everything You Need to Know

content.rendered:
Apple has officially introduced the MacBook Neo, a new entry-level laptop designed to make the Mac ecosystem more accessible to students and first-time users. At a starting price of $599, it’s now the most affordable MacBook Apple has ever released.

Table of Contents
  • MacBook Neo Runs on the A18 Pro Chip
  • Lightweight Design with Colorful Options
  • Display, Ports, and Hardware
  • Up to 16 Hours of Battery Life
  • MacBook Neo Price and Availability
  • Apple’s New Entry Point to macOS

MacBook Neo Runs on the A18 Pro Chip

Unlike the rest of Apple’s Mac lineup, the MacBook Neo is powered by the A18 Pro chip, marking the first time Apple has shipped a Mac running an iPhone-class processor instead of an M-series chip.

Despite the shift, Apple promises smooth performance for everyday tasks such as browsing, streaming, note-taking, and light productivity.

The chip is optimized for common tasks like web browsing, document editing, video playback, and running lightweight apps. For students and casual users, it should provide more than enough power for daily computing needs.

Lightweight Design with Colorful Options

Apple is positioning the MacBook Neo as a fun and approachable Mac.

The laptop comes in four vibrant color options:

  • Silver
  • Indigo
  • Blush
  • Citrus

The design remains thin and lightweight, making it easy to carry to classes, offices, or coffee shops.

Display, Ports, and Hardware

Even though it is Apple’s most affordable MacBook, the Neo still includes several familiar Mac features. The laptop includes:

  • 13-inch Liquid Retina no-notch display
  • Two USB-C ports
  • MagSafe charging
  • A headphone jack
  • A 1080p FaceTime camera
  • Support for Dolby Atmos spatial audio

These additions make it suitable for video calls, entertainment, and everyday productivity.

Up to 16 Hours of Battery Life

Apple claims the MacBook Neo can deliver up to 16 hours of battery life on a single charge. That puts it close to other modern MacBooks and should easily last through a full day of classes or work.

MacBook Neo Price and Availability

The MacBook Neo starts at $599 with 256GB of storage. A higher-tier configuration priced at $699 offers 512GB of storage and Touch ID.

Apple is also offering education pricing starting at $499, making it one of the most affordable ways to get a Mac.

With this launch, Apple now offers a clearer Mac lineup for different users:

  • MacBook Neo for students and casual users
  • MacBook Air with the M5 chip for everyday performance
  • MacBook Pro models for professional workloads

Apple’s New Entry Point to macOS

The MacBook Neo fills a gap that had been growing in Apple’s laptop lineup. As MacBook Air and MacBook Pro models grew more powerful and expensive, Apple lacked a true budget Mac.

By introducing a $599 MacBook, Apple aims to compete more directly with Chromebooks and budget Windows laptops while bringing more users into the macOS ecosystem.

Apple’s MacBook Neo is built for performance and portability. The right accessories can help you unlock its full potential and enhance your daily workflow.
